At #40-46 money was $3, then $0, then -$1, and every shop in ante 5 was unaffordable (#44, #46). At #47 it skipped the Big Blind because a shop would have been useless.
lessons.cost: No interest from ante 4 on, and no buying power in the three shops before The Arm, where a found xMult or Uranus could still have helped.

lessons.rule: Don't swap one flat +Mult or +Chips joker for another as a survival fix. A sideways swap only counts if the outlook rises after it. If the board has no xMult, the money should go to finding xMult (packs or rerolls spread across shops) or to main-hand planets, not to reshuffling flat jokers.
lessons.evidence: #27 sold Hit the Road. #29 swapped Sly for Jolly: the boss stayed at 25%. #31 swapped Even Steven for Mad: the boss fell from 15% to 10%. #28 and #30 rerolled for $11 in one shop. The playbook says to spread rerolls across shops. The boss chance went 25%, 15%, 10% over these moves.
lessons.cost: About $17 of the $31 bought no improvement at all. It was enough for two Celestial packs or about three Uranus.

lessons.rule: If you carry a rental, keep the playbook's $28 floor, not $25. Only take a rental chips joker before ante 3 if it is a core scorer you would still want at ante 5. Count the $3/round as part of the joker's price (about $15-20 over the rest of a short run).
lessons.evidence: #17 bought the Clever Joker rental at ante 2. After that, money sat at $25 (#24-25), below the $28 the playbook asks for with one rental. The rental charged $3 in each of about 6 rounds, and in ante 5 that pushed money from $0 to -$1 (#46).
lessons.cost: About $18 drained over the run. It also left no cushion once money ran low, which helped turn an underpowered board into a run that could not buy anything.

lessons.rule: Commit to Pair as the default main hand unless there is a real signal for something else (Spare Trousers, Mad, Clever already owned, or a planet supply). Don't let one off-plan planet from a pack decide the hand. With only 2 discards, Pair is easier to level and easier to find support jokers for (Jolly, Sly, Duo).
lessons.evidence: #9 picked Uranus only because Mercury was missing, and #14 doubled down. That steered later buys toward Two Pair-only jokers (Clever #17, Mad #31) and made the strategist sell the Pair chips joker Sly (#29). Pair stayed at level 1 all game, so the jokers and the planets were spread across two hands.
lessons.cost: Fewer usable shop options and a split engine. Two Pair at level 5 by ante 5 was still far below the 6-9 target.

summary: The run died to The House at ante 4. The board had four flat +Mult jokers (Abstract, Misprint, eternal Joker, Green), little chips (Castle stuck at 18), Pair only at level 2, and its only multiplier was a polychrome Blueprint rental that arrived one blind before the boss. From decision 13 on, the outlook warned two antes ahead that the next ante would collapse. The strategist answered with low-value rerolls and more flat Mult. It never bought planets or chips, and money stayed between $8 and $18 for the whole run, so there was never surplus to buy the engine. The best hand was about 3.5-4.5k against an 18k boss, a gap no last-shop purchase could close.

lessons.rule: Before buying any scoring joker, compare the board's typical chips and Mult on the main hand and buy for the smaller one. Once Mult is above about 30 and chips are under about 100, another +Mult joker is nearly worthless. Buy chips (main-hand planets, Stuntman, Hiker, Blue Joker, Square, Ice Cream, Bull) or xMult instead, and skip flat +Mult even when it is free.
lessons.evidence: Decisions 22 (Misprint), 28 (eternal Joker taken over other options) and 30 (Green Joker) stacked a fourth and fifth +Mult source. By decision 47 a normal Pair scored about 63 chips x 57 Mult (about 3.6k). Doubling the 63 chips would have doubled the score. Adding Mult barely moved it, which is why the outlook for ante 4 Big/Boss stayed at 5-15% / 0-10% after each pickup.
lessons.cost: Three joker slots (one locked by eternal) went to flat Mult while chips stayed at about 60-80. Ante 4 lost about 4x of score from this imbalance, and the run ended at 11 blinds.

lessons.rule: Do not hold scaling jokers that pull against each other on discards. Banner and Green Joker want zero discards, and Castle wants many. Pick one direction when you buy the second one, and sell or skip the one that conflicts.
lessons.evidence: Decision 5 bought Castle next to Banner, and decision 30 added Green Joker. Rounds 32, 34, 40 and 50 all told the round player not to discard to grow Green. Castle stayed at 18 chips from ante 3 to the end, which made it a dead slot and left the board with no chips source.
lessons.cost: $6 at ante 1 (decision 5 took money from $9 to $3 and blocked the $6 Celestial Jumbo at decision 6). It also cost a permanent slot that should have been a chips or xMult joker.

lessons.rule: If the main hand is below the playbook level target (2-3 by ante 2, 3-5 by antes 3-4), buy its planet or a Celestial pack before any joker reroll. From ante 2, spend surplus on Celestial packs rather than rerolls whenever the outlook shows a collapse one ante ahead.
lessons.evidence: Only one Mercury was bought in the whole run (decision 11). Pair was still level 2 at ante 4 after 12 plays. Rerolls at 13 ($5, safe ante, $15 to $10), 25 ($5, $14 to $9) and 35-37 ($18 total) found nothing, and no Celestial pack was ever opened. This broke the 'Main hand +6 levels' measured priority.
lessons.cost: About 3 missing Pair levels, worth about +0.6 to +1.3 blinds by the measured table and a matching share of the 4x gap at The House.

lessons.rule: In an ante the outlook already shows as safe, do not reroll or buy when that takes money below the next $5 interest tier. Spend at most one reroll per shop and spread them across shops. Do not burn $18 of escalating rerolls ($5, $6, $7) in one shop.
lessons.evidence: Money never reached $25 before ante 4. Decision 5 went from $9 to $3 at ante 1. Decision 13 rerolled from $15 to $10 in an ante the outlook showed as 100% safe, and decision 25 went from $14 to $9. Then decision 33 left a $18 shop untouched to bank, and decisions 35-37 spent $26 down to $8 in one shop. That left $10 for a last-ditch Grabber (decision 51) instead of $25+ for planets, packs or an xMult at ante 3-4.
lessons.cost: Roughly $10-15 of lost interest over antes 1-3, plus about $15-20 of misspent rerolls. That is enough for 2-3 Celestial packs or one xMult joker, which the playbook rates as the single biggest swing (+2.5 blinds).

summary: The run reached ante 5 with five flat or chip jokers, four of them Eternal, no xMult, and its best hand only at level 2. It lost on the ante 5 Small Blind. The engine was already out of reach by ante 4: from decision 31 on, every outlook put ante 5 Big and Boss at 0-15%. What killed it was decisions 46-49. Four rerolls costing $5, $6, $7 and $8 took the money from $36 to $10. That drained Bull's chips and lowered the Small Blind outlook from 97% to 60%, and the run died on that blind. Underneath that, the playbook's two engines (one xMult, one levelled hand) were never built. Four Eternal locks left no slot to convert, and the agent never committed to the hand it actually played.

lessons.rule: When a joker scales with money held (Bull, Bootstraps), every dollar spent lowers your score. Before each reroll or pack, look at the next-blind outlook after the spend. If the next blind would drop below about 85%, or by more than 5 points, stop spending and play the blind. Survival-overrides-interest means spending to fix the next blind, not spending that breaks it while chasing a later one.
lessons.evidence: Decision 45 at $39: next blind 97%. Then rerolls at decisions 46 ($5, 97%), 47 ($6, 96%), 48 ($7, 92%), 49 ($8 at $18, 84%; the playbook only allows $8-9 rerolls 'with a reason'). Decision 50 left the shop at $10 with the next blind at 73%, and decision 51 played it at 60%. The run died on that Small Blind. Four rerolls in a row found nothing, and the boss read 0-10% the whole time, so the spending could not save the ante anyway.
lessons.cost: The run. Held at about $36, the run had a 97% Small Blind and kept Bull's roughly +70 chips and $5 interest. It ended about 3 blinds early (Small Blind instead of Big or Boss).

lessons.rule: Keep at most 2 Eternal jokers that are not xMult. Never buy an Eternal flat-Mult or chips joker if that makes 3 or more locked slots. Pass on it, or look for a non-Eternal copy, even if it lifts the current blind, unless that blind would otherwise fail. Leave at least 2 slots free to sell into for xMult by ante 5.
lessons.evidence: Decision 7 bought Mystic Summit (Eternal), decision 15 Smiley Face (Eternal), decision 30 Bull (Eternal), decision 45 Misprint (Eternal). At decisions 26-27 the agent correctly turned down an Eternal Swashbuckler for exactly this reason, then broke the rule twice. By ante 5 the only joker it could sell was Runner, its main chips source, so even a found xMult would have been costly to fit (decision 50 also turned down Popcorn because Runner was the only open slot). The Plant also blanked Smiley Face, and it could not be sold.
lessons.cost: There was no room to carry out the playbook's 'antes 5-6: convert' step. The board was locked into flat scoring that topped out around ante 4.

lessons.rule: By ante 3, commit to the hand the round player is actually playing and the jokers support. Then buy every planet for it, and take Meteor or Celestial packs with the money above $25. If the main hand is below level 3 at ante 3 or below 4 at ante 4, buying planets comes before holding interest above $25.
lessons.evidence: The plan said Pair, but Runner (taken at decisions 12 and 19) pushed the round player into Straights: 8 plays against 7 Pairs by ante 5. Pair stayed at level 2 from ante 1 to the end, and Straight got only one Saturn (decision 37). Decision 34 turned down the Meteor Tag (Mega Celestial) at ante 4. At decision 16 the agent sold Runner, then took another Runner from a pack at decision 19. At ante 5 both hands were level 2, against the playbook target of 6-9.
lessons.cost: The second-best measured engine (+1.3 blinds for +6 levels) went unused. Ante 5 chip targets of 25k-50k were out of reach without xMult.

lessons.rule: If the outlook at ante 4 already shows the next ante's Big or Boss below 20% with no xMult on the board, do the xMult search in the ante 4 shops. Spend the surplus above $25 there, while rerolls still cost $5 and there are three shops left. Do not save it all for the first shop of the dying ante, where each reroll costs more than the last.
lessons.evidence: From decision 31 on, the ante 5 Big read 5-15% and the Boss 0%. Yet ante 4 used only two $5 rerolls (decisions 36 and 42), and decisions 33 and 39 left with $27 and $25 to protect interest. Then decisions 46-49 spent $26 in one shop at rising prices.
lessons.cost: The same money spread over the ante 4 shops would have seen more fresh shops at $5 each and kept Bull's chips through the ante 5 Small Blind.

lessons.rule: In ante 1, do not reroll or spend below about $10 (Yellow Deck) unless the next blind would fail. A shop that ends at $1 forces skips and slows the climb to $25.
lessons.evidence: Decision 6 rerolled from $11 to $6 when the Big Blind was already 99%. Decision 7 then spent down to $1. Decision 8 skipped the Big Blind partly because '$1 can buy almost nothing'. The run stayed at $9-19 until the Economy Tag at decision 21.
lessons.cost: About 2 antes of lost interest (roughly $6-8) and a weaker ante 2 shop position. It was small next to the losses above, but it was the start of the Eternal locks.

summary: The run died at the ante 4 Big Blind (13,500). It reached ante 4 with no xMult joker, Pair at level 2, and $1. Through antes 1-3 it bought flat, conditional and perishable +Mult (Lusty, Misprint, Blue Joker, Mystic Summit, Abstract) and kept swapping jokers sideways, so money never reached $25. It also turned down the only xMult it was offered (Acrobat, and Vampire twice) because of the rental/eternal stickers. From ante 2 the outlook kept saying the ante 3-4 bosses were 0-35%, but the spending never went toward what would fix that: a multiplier and levels on one hand.

lessons.rule: When the board has no xMult by ante 2-3 and the outlook for an upcoming boss is below 50%, an affordable xMult joker beats any flat +Mult option, even if it has a rental or eternal sticker. One rental is allowed: hold $28 to cover it. Only refuse it if you already carry a rental or it truly cannot fire for your hand.
lessons.evidence: #15: turned down Acrobat (x3 on the final hand, works with any hand) for perishable Mystic Summit because it was 'Eternal + Rental, which the playbook rules out'. The playbook does not ban this; it says Yellow Deck can carry one rental. #16 and #47 turned down Vampire on the same grounds. Every later outlook read 0-35% for the ante 3-4 bosses because nothing on the board multiplied.
lessons.cost: The playbook's top-ranked fix (+2.5 blinds, x15 wins) was offered at ante 2 and left in the pack. The run reached ante 4 with only flat Mult and lost.

lessons.rule: Do not sell one flat or conditional joker to buy another of the same kind. Only make a swap if it adds a multiplier, a lasting chips source your deck actually triggers, or a scaler you will feed for several antes. Never buy a joker that needs card types you don't have (for example Stone Joker with no Stone cards) just to raise the joker count.
lessons.evidence: #24 sold Blue Joker for Stone Joker (0 Stone cards). #27 sold Stone Joker for Wily. #37 sold Lusty for Jolly, and #38 sold Jolly for Ride the Bus right away, which took money from $10 to $5 before the boss. Four swaps in two antes, and the board was no stronger at the end.
lessons.cost: About $10-12 lost to sell-value gaps, plus the interest that money would have earned. It also left $5 at the ante 3 boss, so ante 4 started with $13 and nothing to spend on finding xMult.

lessons.rule: Pick Pair as the main hand by the end of ante 1, and buy or use every Mercury, plus a Celestial pack when $25 is already covered, until Pair reaches level 3 by ante 3 and level 4-5 by ante 4. Stop playing Straights, Full Houses and High Cards that spread the play count around.
lessons.evidence: #12 and #16 skipped Celestial packs ('only 25% to show Mercury'). Only one Mercury was ever bought (#22, ante 3). Hand history shows Straight played 3 times, Two Pair 3, High Card 3 and Full House 2, while Pair was at level 2 by ante 4. #36 also skipped Telescope because Pair wasn't the most-played hand.
lessons.cost: Missed the playbook's second-ranked engine (+1.3 blinds for +6 levels). With no xMult and no levels, 13,500 was out of reach.

lessons.rule: In antes 1-2, Buffoon packs and rerolls are worth buying only if they come with a plan to reach $25 by ante 3. Once the outlook shows a boss collapse two antes out, stop buying perishable stopgaps from packs. Save the money for xMult and planets, or take a non-perishable scorer even if it is slightly weaker now.
lessons.evidence: #2, #9, #14 and #18 bought four Buffoon packs ($22), and #6, #11, #21, #28 and #36 were five $5 rerolls. Money peaked at $23 and never reached the $25 tier. #10 and #15 took perishable Blue Joker and Mystic Summit, and both expired right at the ante 3 boss / ante 4, which caused the very cliff the outlook had flagged.
lessons.cost: Interest stayed at $1-2 a round instead of $5, and ante 4 began with $13. It also left two dead joker slots at the moment the blinds jumped 3x.

lessons.rule: When the board can't survive and you are nearly broke, do not spend your last money on a voucher and then skip a blind. Spend it on things that change the board in the current shop (packs, rerolls aimed at xMult). Skip a blind only when the tag directly fixes the next blind.
lessons.evidence: #48 spent $10 of $11 on Grabber. #50 then skipped the Small Blind at $1 for a Coupon Tag whose free shop would only arrive after the Big Blind. #51 played the Big Blind at 45% with no new scoring, and the run died at #52.
lessons.cost: Gave up the last shop and the last $10 that could have dug for xMult before the 13,500 Big Blind. The run ended there.

summary: The run got through antes 1-4 on flat jokers (Banner, Green Joker, Shoot the Moon, Even Steven, Lusty) and died at the ante 5 boss, The Wheel. It never had an xMult joker and Pair was still level 2. Two things decided it. First, the strategist filled four of its five joker slots with Eternal flat jokers, so by ante 5 no slot was left to convert into xMult. Second, it spent about $61 on 11 rerolls that never found xMult, while buying only one Mercury and turning down Celestial packs. That cost both the planet engine and the $25 interest bank, and ante 5 ended with $2 and a board scoring about 1-2k per hand against a 50,000 target.

lessons.rule: Keep at least 2 joker slots that can be sold (not Eternal) from ante 3 on. Do not buy an Eternal flat +Mult or +Chips joker if it would make 3 or more slots Eternal, unless the next blind reads below 60% without it and there is no non-Eternal option that does as well. Before buying any Eternal, ask: 'when the xMult shows up, which slot does it go in?'
lessons.evidence: Banner [eternal] at #7, Shoot the Moon [eternal] at #32, Even Steven [eternal] at #45 (sold Scary Face to make room), Lusty [eternal] at #48 (sold Sly to make room). By ante 5 the only sellable joker was Green Joker (+24-27 Mult). At #57, #62 and #63, Photograph, Supernova and other picks were turned down because the only way to take them was to sell Green. The strategist itself noted that the build needed 'an xMult in Green Joker's slot' (#49, #53), and that slot was also its best scorer.
lessons.cost: The board could not change from ante 4 on, so the playbook's 'antes 5-6: convert' step was impossible. Each Eternal bought a few % on one boss and gave up the run's whole ceiling.

lessons.rule: When the main hand is below the playbook's level target (2-3 by ante 2, 3-5 by antes 3-4), buy every planet for that hand and open a Celestial pack before paying for a 2nd reroll in the same shop. Levels are guaranteed, measured scoring (+0.6 blinds per 3 levels). Rerolls for xMult are a gamble.
lessons.evidence: Pair went from level 1 to only level 2 in the whole run, with one Mercury at #23. Celestial packs were passed over at #8, #12, #25 ('Celestial Mega Pack' at $16) and #40. Meanwhile the rerolls at #21-22, #29-31, #35-36 and #51-52 (about $50 at ante 3 and later) found no xMult. At ante 5 Pair was level 2 against a target of 6-9.
lessons.cost: The second engine was missing. Five or six more Pair levels would have roughly doubled or tripled each hand's base score and could have carried ante 5 Big. Instead the run hit the wall at about 2k per hand against a 25k-50k target.

lessons.rule: Rerolling for xMult: at most 2 rerolls per shop, and never below $20 unless the NEXT blind (not a forecast two antes out) reads below 70%. A bad forecast for later antes is a reason to keep interest and buy planets, not to empty the bank on rerolls.
lessons.evidence: #29-31 spent $18 on three rerolls in one shop ($41 to $23) because of the ante 4 forecast. #35-36 went from $25 to $14 while the next blind was 99-100%. #51-52 went from $18 to $7 while the next blind was 97%. The $32 from the Economy Tag (#26) was gone within one shop. The run held $25 at round end only once or twice.
lessons.cost: About $61 on rerolls and about $3-4 a round of lost interest through antes 3-5. With no money left at ante 5 ($2-8), the last shops could buy nothing.

lessons.rule: Do not buy a Buffoon pack when every joker slot is full and the only sellable joker is a key scorer, unless you would actually sell that joker for an xMult. Decide before paying what you would sell, and spend the money on a planet or on interest instead.
lessons.evidence: #56: spent $6 of $8 on a Buffoon Jumbo, then skipped every pick (#57) because only Green could be sold. #61: spent $4 of $6 on a Buffoon Normal and skipped again (#62).
lessons.cost: $10 of the last $14 brought nothing, which left $2 and no options at the Big Blind and the boss.

summary: The run died at the ante 5 Small Blind (25,000 chips). By then the board had no xMult joker, Pair was still level 1, and only $2 was left. Antes 1-2 were safe, but about $43 went on eight rerolls in antes 2-3 that found nothing. Planets for Pair were never bought, so money never reached $25. At decision 50 the only multiplier, Card Sharp (x3), was sold for Supernova to gain 9 points on the ante 4 boss, which left ante 5 with no answer.

lessons.rule: Do not sell your only xMult joker for a flat or scaling +Mult joker unless the boss you are about to face is impossible with it. Before any swap that removes a multiplier, compare the next ante's outlook with and without the swap, not just the next blind. Paying $3 a round in rent for an x3 joker is cheap.
lessons.evidence: 36: Card Sharp (x3, $1 rental) took The Fish from 24% to 82%. 50: it was sold for Supernova because the engine rated The Mark at 24% → 33%. 56: Supernova was then sold for a perishable Half Joker. At ante 5 the board had no xMult, the Small Blind read 12-18% and the boss 0%. Playbook item #1 says one xMult joker is worth +2.5 blinds.
lessons.cost: It removed the one piece that could have scaled into ante 5. Every ante 5 shop afterwards read 0% for the boss.

lessons.rule: In antes 1-3, when every blind in the current ante reads 90% or better, do not reroll below $25 because of a low reading for a boss one or two antes away. Bank toward $25 and spend only the surplus. Count 'survival before interest' only for the current ante's blinds, or for the next one when it reads below 70%.
lessons.evidence: 11, 12, 15, 20, 23 (ante 2, every blind 100%) and 26, 27, 30 (ante 3, next blind 85-99%): eight rerolls cost about $43 and turned up only Mime (31). Money dropped to $10-11 again and again, and interest never went above $3. 'Survival first' was cited each time, but the threat was always a later boss.
lessons.cost: About $43 in rerolls plus several dollars a round in lost interest. That is roughly two xMult jokers or 6+ Pair levels. The run reached ante 4 with $5 (43) and ante 5 with $2-8.

lessons.rule: From ante 2, if the main hand is below the playbook target (level 2-3 by ante 2, 3-5 by antes 3-4), buy Mercury on sight and choose a Celestial pack over a reroll. If the main hand's planet keeps not showing up by ante 3, think about moving to the hand whose planets you are being offered.
lessons.evidence: Celestial packs were passed at 10, 28, 30, 33 and 43, mostly because the odds of Mercury looked low. Rerolls were bought instead, with odds that were just as poor. Pair was level 1 for the whole run, even after being played 8 times. The one Celestial Jumbo opened (48) came at ante 4 with $22 and missed. Playbook: main hand +6 levels is worth +1.3 blinds and is the second engine.
lessons.cost: Pair scored at its base value against 25,000 at ante 5. Even with Card Sharp kept, a level-1 Pair could not keep up past ante 4.

lessons.rule: Early on, buy jokers that scale or multiply, or plain +Mult. Skip conditional chips and support jokers such as Scary Face, and Mime without a strong held-in-hand card. If a shop has none of the first kind, keep the money for the next shop instead of filling slots.
lessons.evidence: 9: Scary Face (only fires on face cards). 31: Mime, used to retrigger Raised Fist. 47: Scary Face swapped for an eternal Banner. 52-53 and 60-61: Standard packs bought at $7 and $6, leaving $2-3. After all of these the board still scored about 4.7k against 25k (57).
lessons.cost: Slots and $15-20 went into pieces that added little score, and the money was gone when an xMult or Mercury might have shown up.

summary: The run got through antes 1-3 on cheap flat jokers and perishable bridges. It reached ante 4 with $35, Two Pair at level 3 and no xMult joker. In the ante 4 shops it spent most of that money on rerolls, side-grade flat jokers and Celestial packs it then skipped. It found Card Sharp and Flower Pot only in the last two shops, and by the final shop it had $8 left, too little to buy a Two Pair planet or reroll again. It went into The Fish at about 60% (28% once the round started) and lost. What decided the run was spending money that never became lasting scoring, which left too little to back the xMult once it appeared.

lessons.rule: When a boss you must beat is below 50%, do not spend more than about half your money on rerolls in one shop. Stop rerolling once the next reroll would leave less than about $12 for the remaining shops before the boss. Each later shop is a fresh roll for xMult, and you need money there to buy the xMult plus a planet or reroll alongside it.
lessons.evidence: Decisions 44-47: at the first ante 4 shop it had $35. It bought Mystic Summit for $5, then rerolled for $5, $6 and $7, falling to $12 and finding nothing. It then had to use Temperance (48-49) to get money back. The xMult turned up in later shops anyway: Card Sharp at 55 and Flower Pot at 67. At 67-69 it had to sell Sly to afford Flower Pot and was left with $8, which could not pay for a Uranus or another reroll (69).
lessons.cost: About $23 spent in one shop with nothing to show for it. Interest dropped from $5 to $2. In the boss shop there was no money to back Flower Pot with chips or a planet, and the boss stayed at 60%.

lessons.rule: From ante 3 on, do not buy perishable or flat jokers that replace another flat joker (Swashbuckler, Supernova, Riff-Raff for random commons) just because they add a few points to a boss estimate that is still failing. Keep a slot and the money free for an xMult joker or a main-hand planet. Only buy a flat joker if it alone lifts the next blind above about 80%.
lessons.evidence: Decision 27: Riff-Raff for $6 made Credit Card and To Do List, which were sold at 36-37. Riff-Raff itself was sold at 41. Decision 40: a perishable Swashbuckler for $4, sold at 55. Decision 56: Raised Fist sold for a perishable Supernova, which was itself sold at 65 for Blue Joker. Decision 67: Sly sold for Flower Pot. That is four flat jokers bought and sold within about 8 shops.
lessons.cost: Roughly $15-18 lost to buying and reselling at lower value, plus a missed interest tier. That is about the price of one more reroll plus a Uranus in the decisive Fish shop.

lessons.rule: Only open a Celestial pack when your main hand has at least two planets that level it (for example Pair or Two Pair with Mercury or Uranus, and Black Hole) and you would still have at least $15 afterwards. Otherwise, buy the main hand's planet directly when the shop sells it, or keep the money.
lessons.evidence: Decisions 12-13: a $4 pack opened at $15, every card skipped. Decisions 57-58: a $4 pack opened at $11, every card skipped, leaving $7 going into the Big Blind before The Fish. Only 50-51 (Mercury) and the free packs at 18-21 paid off.
lessons.cost: $8 spent for nothing. The pack at 57 cost a reroll in the boss shop and kept money below $10, so interest fell to $1.

lessons.rule: In antes 1-2, do not pay for perishable or off-plan jokers when the current blind is already at 95% or better. Spend only to fix a blind that is actually failing, and use the Yellow Deck head start to reach $25 by the end of ante 2. Do not reroll below $20 in ante 1. This is the playbook rule 'Do not open packs or reroll below about $20-25 in the early antes'.
lessons.evidence: Decision 4: a perishable Devious Joker for $4, a Straight joker on a Pair plan. Decision 8: a $5 reroll at $16 that found nothing and dropped money to $11. Decision 12: the pack that was skipped. As a result it went into ante 3 with $23, missed the ante 2 Small Blind's shop and payout, and needed the emergency buys in ante 3 (27, 40) because both perishables expired at once.
lessons.cost: About $13 spent early with no lasting scoring, plus lost interest in antes 1-2. It reached ante 3 with no lasting joker except the Two Pair-only Mad Joker, and the next two antes went to patching that instead of hunting xMult.

summary: The run ended at the ante 1 Small Blind (300 chips) with no jokers, no shop visit and 0 blinds beaten. The outlook before that blind said 98% to win, so this was almost certainly a play mistake, not bad luck. The log records only decision 1 (choosing to play the blind). No individual hands or discards were logged, so the exact error can't be confirmed. The likeliest cause is that the strategist followed its plan note's "Pair as the default main hand" with an empty board. At level 1, no Pair can reach 300 in 4 hands: Pair of Aces scores 64, so four of them make 256.

lessons.rule: When you have no scoring jokers (antes 1-2 before the first shop buy), don't play Pair as your main hand. Each hand must average blind ÷ hands remaining: 75 for a 300 blind over 4 hands. Level-1 Pair tops out around 64 and Two Pair around 60-80. Use both discards to build Three of a Kind (about 90-130), a Straight (about 200-260) or a Flush (about 250-300). Play a Pair only when it is the last hand and it finishes the blind. The playbook's 'Default: Pair' applies once you have +Mult or chips jokers, not on a blank board.
lessons.evidence: Decision 1: the Small Blind was played with 'Jokers: none' and all hands at level 1. The plan note said 'Pair as the default main hand.' The run died at this blind despite a 98% outlook. With no jokers, even four Pairs of Aces score 256 < 300, so playing for Pairs from the start can't win this blind.
lessons.cost: The whole run: 0 blinds beaten, and the $14 Yellow Deck head start never reached a shop.

lessons.rule: Before each hand, work out the running total: chips still needed and hands left. If the best hand you can play now won't keep you on pace (needed ÷ hands left), discard toward a bigger hand while discards remain, even if that means giving up a pair you already hold. With only 2 discards at Gold, use both early in the round, while there are still hands left to play what they dig up.
lessons.evidence: A 98%-outlook blind was lost on an empty board. That only happens if hands keep falling behind the 75-per-hand pace and the discards are wasted or saved too long. No hand-level decisions were logged after decision 1, which suggests the hands were played without this check.
lessons.cost: Turned a near-certain win (98%) into elimination in ante 1.

lessons.rule: Treat losing a blind rated 90% or higher as a play error and audit it. Log every hand and discard with cards played, score and running total, so the specific mistake can be found and fixed.
lessons.evidence: Only decision 1 was logged for this game. The cause of a 2%-risk loss can't be pinned down from the record.
lessons.cost: Without hand-by-hand logs, the same scoring mistake can keep ending runs in ante 1 without being diagnosed.

summary: The run died on the first blind: 0 blinds beaten, lost the Ante 1 Small Blind (300 chips) with no jokers. The only logged decision (#1, play the Small Blind instead of skipping for the Foil Tag) was correct and consistent with the playbook, and its outlook gave a 98% chance to clear. So the loss came from how the hands and discards were played, not from strategy. The log has no hand or discard decisions at all, so the exact misplay can't be pinned down. The lessons below are about playing a jokerless opening blind and recording those decisions, and they rest on thin evidence.

lessons.rule: On a blind with no jokers, before each hand work out chips still needed ÷ hands left. A level-1 Pair (about 30-60 points) does not reach the roughly 75-point average that 300 chips in 4 hands requires. Use both discards early, while 3-4 hands remain, to dig for Two Pair or better (Three of a Kind about 180, Straight about 260, Flush about 300). Do not play a lone Pair or High Card while discards are left unless that hand alone keeps you on pace.
lessons.evidence: Decision 1's outlook gave the Small Blind 98%, yet the run lost it with 0 blinds beaten. No later decisions were logged. With no jokers and every hand at level 1, a 98% blind is only lost when weak hands are played early and discards are saved or wasted. A 2% event is possible, but the more likely cause is base hands that fell short of the needed pace.
lessons.cost: The whole run. It ended at the first blind, before any shop.

lessons.rule: Record every play and discard as its own numbered decision, with the expected score, chips still needed and hands/discards left. If the score after hand 2 is below 50% of the target, switch to the highest-variance line available, such as discarding toward a Flush or Straight, rather than continuing with Pairs.
lessons.evidence: The log ends after decision 1 (blind select), so the decisions that actually lost the run, the 4 hands and 2 discards in the Small Blind, cannot be seen or corrected. Every playbook rule covers shops, economy and building. None covers how to play hands inside a blind, and that is where this run was lost.
lessons.cost: The cause can't be diagnosed from this log, and the same failure can happen again without anyone noticing.

lessons.rule: Treat win chances for blinds played with no jokers as less reliable than the number suggests. If the forecast hits a miss partway through, such as a weak first hand, drop the shop-planning mindset and play only for the blind's chip target.
lessons.evidence: Decision 1 was argued entirely around the coming shop (find a first scorer, keep interest) and treated the Small Blind as already won at 98%. The run then lost that blind outright.
lessons.cost: Overconfidence in a 'free' blind ended the run before it started.

summary: The run died at the ante 1 boss, The Head (600 chips). It won only the Small Blind. The board was a single suit-conditional rental joker (Wrathful, +3 Mult per scored Spade) from a $4 Buffoon pack. The strategist then skipped the Big Blind for an Investment Tag on the outlook's 95% boss read. Skipping gave up a shop, $4 and a chance to see how the board actually scored before the boss. In effect it risked the whole run for about $19 of net value. A 1-joker board that only scores on Spades, against a boss that debuffs Hearts, was riskier than the 95% suggested, and losing it ended the run.

lessons.rule: In antes 1-2, do not skip a blind for an economy tag (Investment, Economy, etc.) unless the board has at least one joker that adds Mult or chips on every hand with no condition, and the boss outlook is 98% or higher. A skip removes the last shop before the boss. Only take it when the boss is beaten even if one card or suit goes wrong.
lessons.evidence: Decision 5: skipped the Big Blind for the Investment Tag with only Wrathful (a Spades-only rental) on the board, citing boss 95%. The run then lost to The Head, so the Big Blind shop and payout that could have bought a second scorer never came.
lessons.cost: The run. The expected gain was about +$19 by ante 2. The stake was a run-ending loss at the first boss.

lessons.rule: Lower the outlook in your head when the whole board is one conditional joker (suit, rank or hand-type), and lower it more when the boss debuffs cards or cuts hand options. Treat a 95% read on that board as about 85% when deciding whether to skip, reroll or leave a shop without a buy.
lessons.evidence: Decisions 3-5: the boss read went from 65% to 95% based entirely on Wrathful, which only fires on 13 of 52 cards. The Head debuffed Hearts as well, which made the useful draws even thinner. The 95% did not hold up.
lessons.cost: Overconfidence in one bridge joker caused both the skip and the empty shop exit at decision 4.

lessons.rule: The playbook's 'Investment Tag in ante 1 is a good skip' advice needs a precondition: a solid board (at least 2 scoring jokers, or 1 that scores on every hand plus a planet for the main hand). Without that, play the Big Blind, take the shop, and save skips for when the ante is overbuilt. The strategist's own plan note already said 'No more skips'. Apply that rule from ante 1 whenever the board is thin.
lessons.evidence: Decision 5's reasoning leaned on the playbook naming this as the one recommended skip. The playbook also lists 'skipped blinds' as a known failure of the previous agent. With an empty-plus-rental board, the recommendation was applied in exactly the situation it shouldn't cover.
lessons.cost: Turned a small economy edge into a first-ante loss.

summary: The run died to The Goad, the ante 1 boss, without ever owning a joker that scored. When it was played the outlook put the boss at about 82%, so the loss was a risk the strategist could see, not bad luck. Every outlook along the way also put ante 2 at 0-20%. The strategist turned down Half Joker for Red Card, which was worth nothing. It left two shops without spending, to protect $14-15 under the "don't reroll below $20 when the next blind is safe" rule. Its only scoring buy was Photograph, a perishable that only fires on face cards. The board stayed empty while the boss chance sat at 70-85%, and that decided the run.

lessons.rule: In antes 1-2 with no scoring joker, take the joker that adds score now over a scaling joker that starts at 0, even if it is a rental. The 'no rentals in ante 1' rule applies only when the board can already clear the ante boss above ~90% and ante 2 Small above ~50%. Yellow Deck can carry one rental.
lessons.evidence: #3: the strategist took Red Card (+0, and it grows only when packs are skipped) over Half Joker. It cited the no-rental lesson even though the boss read 70% and ante 2 read 5-15%. Red Card was never fed: no pack was skipped afterwards, so it scored 0 for the rest of the run.
lessons.cost: Half Joker's +20 Mult on every Pair would probably have pushed The Goad well above 82% and given ante 2 a real chance. Red Card added nothing.

lessons.rule: Before turning a joker down, check its condition against your main hand. With Pair as the main hand, anything that fires on hands of 3 or fewer cards fires on every Pair. Jokers tied to face cards (Photograph) fire only on some Pairs, so they are weaker than they look.
lessons.evidence: #3 rejected Half Joker as 'only fires on plays of 3 or fewer cards', but a Pair is 2 cards. #7 then spent $5 of $20 on a perishable Photograph, which only works on face-card Pairs, and The Goad debuffed Spades on top of that (#9).
lessons.cost: The strategist turned down a joker that always fires and paid for one that fires sometimes. It also dropped from $20 to $15.

lessons.rule: Judge 'safe' on the boss and the next ante, not only on the next blind. If the outlook shows the current boss under 85% or the next ante's Small Blind under 30%, the money rules give way: reroll or buy packs down to ~$5-8 to find a scorer, even in ante 1.
lessons.evidence: #4 left the shop at $14 because the Big Blind read 97%, while the boss read 75% and ante 2 was failing. #8 left at $15 with ante 2 at 20%/0% and the boss at 86%, passing on a reroll. The playbook's 'survival overrides interest' should have applied, since the projected death was 1-2 blinds away.
lessons.cost: Two or three rerolls were skipped to protect interest worth about $1-3 in total. The run then died one blind later with $15 unspent.

lessons.rule: If you keep a joker that grows on a trigger you control, feed it on purpose. For Red Card, open and skip cheap packs whenever no card in them is worth more than +3 Mult. Otherwise don't keep it while you lack scoring.
lessons.evidence: #4 passed on a Standard pack and #8 on 'one-card tweak' packs. Either could have been bought and skipped for +3 Mult on Red Card, its only use.
lessons.cost: Red Card stayed at +0 Mult through the boss fight.

summary: The run died at the ante 4 boss (The Fish, 18,000) after 11 blinds. It never found an xMult joker. Its main hand, Two Pair, was only level 2, below the playbook's target of 3-5, and its board was Mad Joker plus flat filler. The outlook warned about this from ante 2 (ante 3 boss at 10%, ante 4 boss at 15%). The bot answered by skipping Small Blinds for D6 tags and spending about $29 on rerolls that found nothing. It turned down affordable scorers and planets while joker slots sat empty. Then at ante 4 it panic-bought rentals until it had $5 and was paying $9 a round in rent.

lessons.rule: Keep a reroll budget. If $10 of rerolls in one ante has not turned up an xMult, put the rest of the surplus into the main hand's planets (Celestial packs, single planets) until the hand reaches its level target. Levels are guaranteed progress; rerolls are a lottery. Never turn down a Celestial pack while the main hand is below target and the purchase keeps you at $20 or more.
lessons.evidence: Rerolls at 7 ($5), 16-17 ($3), 24-28 ($10), 30 ($5), 33 ($6) and 39 ($5) cost about $34 and produced no xMult; nothing bought came from them. Only two Celestial packs were opened (9 and 19), and pack 9 gave Mercury, a planet for an off-plan hand. The Celestial Mega pack was passed at 4. Two Pair entered ante 4 at level 2 against a target of 3-5.
lessons.cost: About $30, which could have bought 4-6 more Two Pair levels (the playbook measures +3 levels at about +0.6 blinds). The Fish then needed roughly a 3x jump that no single shop could supply.

lessons.rule: Do not skip a Small Blind for a D6 (or similar reroll) tag when the board lacks scoring. A skip gives up a whole shop, the unused-hand money and an interest round, and the D6 rerolls that come back are still a lottery. Skip only for an Investment tag, or when the board already clears the next two bosses.
lessons.evidence: The bot skipped for a D6 tag at 12 and again at 22. The tag rerolls (14, 16-17, 24-28) found only Bootstraps. Both skips were made while the outlook showed the following ante's boss at 10-15%. The playbook lists skipping blinds as one of the previous agent's failures.
lessons.cost: Two shops' worth of looks and about $6-8 in hand money and interest. That is exactly the shop access the run needed to find a multiplier or planets before ante 4.

lessons.rule: With empty joker slots and money above $25, buy durable flat scorers that fit the hand (Raised Fist, Castle, Greedy or Sly types) in antes 2-3. Do not pass on them while waiting for an xMult. A filled board buys time to find the multiplier, and it avoids buying rentals in a panic later.
lessons.evidence: The bot passed Raised Fist at 21 and 27, Runner at 26, Castle at 29 and Greedy at 36. The board stayed at 3 of 5 jokers through ante 3. Then at ante 4 it bought Even Steven (31), a Popcorn rental (32) and a Sly Joker rental (40) in an emergency.
lessons.cost: The board reached the ante 4 boss with weaker, decaying and rented scorers in place of steady ones bought earlier with surplus money.

lessons.rule: Follow the rental rules strictly: no third rental, and with two rentals stop rerolling and hold $31. Count the $3 per rental per round as a recurring cost before buying a $1 rental. Do not buy rentals that are also perishable or decaying, such as Popcorn.
lessons.evidence: The bot bought a Blue Joker rental at 8, then a Popcorn rental (which loses 4 Mult a round) at 32, and rerolled for $6 at 33 and $5 at 39 while holding two rentals. It added a third rental, Sly, at 40. Money fell from $28 to $5 over ante 4.
lessons.cost: $9 a round in rent, no interest, and no money left to act in a later shop. Even surviving The Fish would have left the run unable to buy anything in ante 5.

lessons.rule: Do not buy money-scaling jokers (Bootstraps, Bull) on a plan that spends heavily on rerolls. Either commit to holding $25+ so they pay off, or skip them.
lessons.evidence: The bot bought Bootstraps for $7 at 15 (about +10 Mult at $25), then spent money down through rerolls and rentals. At $8 it was worth about +2 Mult, and it was sold at 38 for about $3.
lessons.cost: About $4 lost on the trade, plus the bigger cost of Bootstraps being nearly worthless at the moment the run needed Mult most.

summary: The run never had a lasting multiplier or any money to spare, and it died to The Arm in ante 4 with Pair at level 4 and only flat face-card jokers plus an expiring Ramen. Antes 1-2 were survived on chips jokers. The money was then wasted: $8 on The Order, which only fires on Straights and was sold a few shops later; money fell to $1; and two rentals (Seltzer, Ramen) charged $6 a round. Money then stayed at $5-13 for all of antes 3-4. That made rerolls and packs impossible in exactly the antes where the playbook says to dig for xMult. The Rare Tag skip in ante 3 apparently paid nothing because all joker slots were full.

lessons.rule: Do not buy a conditional xMult joker (The Order, The Tribe, The Family, etc.) whose hand you are not committed to and cannot draw reliably (Straight with no Shortcut or Four Fingers). This applies even more when the purchase drops you below $10. When the boss reads below 30% and there is no Mult, the $8 should go to rerolls or a joker that fires on the main hand.
lessons.evidence: #12 bought The Order for $8 at $13 (boss 10%). The board played Pair, so The Order gave no help against The House. #13-15 left $1, so the Big Blind shop (#18-19) had nothing to spend. #30 sold The Order to make room for Ramen, and the engine said selling it alone raised the boss from 60% to 70%. The joker was dead weight from the moment it was bought.
lessons.cost: About $8 lost plus a whole ante with no interest ($1-5 in ante 2). The two ante 2 shops were wasted, and this is a direct reason the board reached the boss shop still needing three rerolls and a Jumbo pack.

lessons.rule: Carry at most one rental before ante 5. If a second rental is the only survival fix, plan to sell one at the next shop where the next blind reads at least 85% without it. Do not leave both in place across an ante while money is below $31, which is the playbook's two-rental threshold.
lessons.evidence: #26 Seltzer (rental) and #30 Ramen (rental + perishable) together charged $6 a round. Ante 3 opened at $13 and dropped to $9 (#36). #40 left the shop at $8 because of rent. #44-45 had $5-9, and every pack or reroll was refused because 'rent is due'. Only one reroll (#49) happened in antes 3-4. Ramen expired in ante 4 anyway.
lessons.cost: Roughly $15-18 of rent over antes 3-4. Money never got back near $25, so interest was lost. With no rerolls or packs in antes 3-4, the run never found the xMult it needed for ante 4. The playbook's 'no rerolls for 2-3 antes means the run is in trouble' warning came true.

lessons.rule: Before skipping a blind for a joker tag (Rare, Uncommon, Holographic, Foil, etc.), check that a joker slot will be free in the shop where the tag pays out. In that shop, always look at the free joker and sell the weakest or expiring joker (spent Seltzer, decaying Ice Cream, economy) to take it if it scores better. Otherwise the skip gives up a blind's payout and a shop for nothing.
lessons.evidence: #37 skipped the ante 3 Small Blind for the Rare Tag with all 5 slots full (Smiley, Jolly, Scary, Seltzer, Ramen). The next shop (#40) says 'all 5 slots are full' and left without taking any free Rare. A nearly used-up Seltzer could have been sold to make room. #51 skipped the ante 4 Big Blind for a Holographic Tag that never paid out, because the next round was the losing boss.
lessons.cost: A free Rare joker in ante 3 was the run's best chance at a real multiplier before the ante 4 cliff. The ante 4 skip also gave up a shop and $4+ while the board had 33% on the Big Blind.

lessons.rule: Once the outlook shows the next boss at 10% or less and the next ante at 0%, stop buying economy jokers. Every dollar goes to rerolls, packs, or planets aimed at a multiplier, and a perishable or rental expiring this ante should be treated as already gone when you plan.
lessons.evidence: #44 spent $4 of $9 on a perishable Business Card while The Arm read 5%. #48 then sold it to free a slot. The reasoning at #44 rejected a reroll because it 'would leave $1', and the $4 went to economy instead. Ramen's expiry after the Big Blind was known from ante 3 (#39), but nothing was ever bought to replace its x2.
lessons.cost: About $4 and one shop's choice in the last ante. It also made a reroll unaffordable at the point where only an xMult could save the run.

summary: The run used the Investment Tag well and reached ante 2 with $50. Most of that money then went on stopgaps that were replaced one shop later: perishable Odd Todd, Lusty Joker, and the Ramen rental from the skip for a free pack. In ante 3 the build switched to The Trio (x3 on Three of a Kind), but the deck never got any rank shaping and still had 2 discards. Three of a Kind stayed hard to draw. At ante 4 the board was one conditional xMult plus flat jokers. On the last decision before the 9,000 Small Blind (#50), the strategist sold Banner. That dropped the next-blind read from 100% to 84% (73% when the blind was chosen), and the run died on that blind.

lessons.rule: In the last shop before a blind, never sell a scoring joker if the outlook for that blind goes down afterward. This applies even more with Abstract Joker on the board, since every joker sold also removes +3 Mult. Accept a lower boss read only if the next blind still reads 95% or more after the sale. A boss estimate means nothing if you die on the blind in front of it.
lessons.evidence: #50 sold Banner for $2 because the engine said the boss would rise from 52% to 59%. Before the sale the Small Blind read 100% (#41-49). Right after it read 84% (#51), then 73% at blind select (#52), then 61% and 51% during the round (#53-54). The run died on that Small Blind.
lessons.cost: Probably the run. The blind it died on had read 100% before the sale.

lessons.rule: If your only xMult needs a hand that is hard to draw with 2 discards (The Trio / Three of a Kind, The Family, Four of a Kind), shape the deck right away. Take Strength, Death or Hanged Man to pile cards onto a few ranks, and keep a scorer for the hand you actually draw most until the deck can make the target hand. Otherwise prefer the playbook's default, Pair.
lessons.evidence: #22 committed to The Trio. #39 sold Mad Joker, which powered Two Pair, the hand played 5 times against 1 for Three of a Kind. #48 passed on Death/Strength as 'a small effect'. At ante 4 the deck was still 52 cards spread evenly across ranks, and the round needed 3-card Three of a Kinds that kept failing to show up (#53-55).
lessons.cost: The x3 rarely fired. The Small Blind at ante 4 read near a coin flip during play.

lessons.rule: If the current ante already reads 80% or more and the danger is the next ante, do not buy stopgaps: perishables, small conditional +Mult, rentals, or skips for packs that only hand you perishables. Spend only on lasting pieces (xMult, main-hand planets, deck shaping), and hold $25 from ante 3.
lessons.evidence: #6 Odd Todd (perishable, $4) was sold at #22. #17 Lusty ($5) was sold one shop later at #21. #11 skipped a blind for the free Mega Buffoon Pack and got Ramen (perishable rental), sold at #23. Ante 2 went from $50 to $29, and ante 3 went from $39 to $18 (#20-27). So at #33 there was 'no surplus' to look for the second xMult.
lessons.cost: About $15-20 spent on pieces that did not last, interest lost below $25, and fewer rerolls and packs at ante 4 when the build needed them.

lessons.rule: Treat outlook changes of less than about 10 points as noise. Do not trade a known, lasting effect (a joker, a slot, a blind's payout) for a small simulated gain. Re-check the move against the next blind's read, not only the boss.
lessons.evidence: In ante 4 the boss read swung between 40% and 65% from shop to shop while the board barely changed (#42-51). #50 sold Banner because of a 7-point simulated boss gain, which is inside that swing.
lessons.cost: It led to the fatal sale of Banner.

summary: The run had money early: the Investment Tag put it at $48 at the start of ante 2. It spent that on rerolls (about $40 over antes 2-4) and on an eternal rental Loyalty Card. It never found a reliable xMult joker or a second Two Pair planet, so Two Pair stayed at level 3 from ante 3 to ante 5. From ante 3 on, rent, The Tooth's charge per card and more rerolls below the floor drained the money. The second rental (Baseball Card at $5) finished the economy. At ante 5 it had $2, skipped both blinds into The Hook at 10-15%, and died there.

lessons.rule: The rental exception for xMult covers only xMult that fires on every hand (Cavendish, Card Sharp on a repeated hand, Baseball with Uncommons, and so on) and that you can sell. Never buy an eternal rental. Never treat Loyalty Card or another periodic or conditional xMult as 'the multiplier' that justifies paying rent. Before buying any rental, add up $3 times the rounds left (about 20 at ante 2) and compare it with the price of a Celestial pack and a reroll.
lessons.evidence: At decision 8, ante 2 with $32, it bought an eternal rental Loyalty Card (x4 once every 6 hands) and called it the xMult exception. That raised its floor to $28 and blocked other rentals (decisions 9 and 19). It still kept saying the board had 'no real multiplier' (decisions 18, 26, 30, 35, 39). Because Loyalty was eternal it could never be sold to recover money or the slot.
lessons.cost: About $3 a round for roughly 12 rounds (about $36) plus the interest that money would have earned. That is more than enough for 4-5 Celestial packs. It also pushed the run into the second rental that broke the economy.

lessons.rule: If the main hand is below the playbook's level target (3-5 by antes 3-4), spend surplus on Celestial packs and on-plan planets before rerolls. Reroll only after one Celestial look per shop. Cap reroll spending at about $10 per ante unless you hold $60 or more.
lessons.evidence: Rerolls at decisions 6, 7, 18, 19, 24, 29-31, 35 and 39 cost about $40 and turned up Loyalty Card and Fibonacci, no xMult. In all of antes 2-5 it opened one Celestial pack (decision 13, which found Uranus) and skipped the Celestial pack at decision 46. Two Pair stayed at level 3 from ante 3 into ante 5, when the target there is 6-9.
lessons.cost: The second engine (main hand levels, worth about +0.6 blinds per +3 levels) never came online. Ante 4 and ante 5 bosses read 15-30% because of that.

lessons.rule: Pick Pair as the main hand unless a strong signal says otherwise. A common +Mult joker such as Mad Joker is not a signal for Two Pair. If the main hand's planet has not shown up after two antes and Pair jokers are on the board, switch to Pair and buy Mercury.
lessons.evidence: At decision 2 it committed to Two Pair on a $4 Mad Joker. Uranus showed up once in four antes. Mercury was offered at decisions 7, 35 and 49 and turned down each time as 'off-plan', even though Sly Joker (decision 12) fires on any Pair. The playbook says 'Two Pair scores like two separate pairs; prefer Pair.'
lessons.cost: The choice of hand made planets scarce and turned away the planets the shops did offer, which kept the main hand at level 3.

lessons.rule: From ante 3, below $20 do not reroll and do not take on a new rental. With one rental the floor is $28. If money falls below $15 with a rental, the only allowed purchases are ones the outlook shows fix the next blind. Against The Tooth, count its $1 per card into the money plan and play 4-card Two Pairs, or as few hands as possible.
lessons.evidence: At decision 35 it rerolled from $15 to $10, and at decision 39 from $10 to $5. Both broke the rule against rerolling below $20-25. At decision 40 it took a second rental at $5, which breaks the playbook's 'with two rentals hold $31'. Rent of $6 a round then forced The Hermit and Tower plays (decisions 43-45) and left $2 at ante 5 (decisions 50-54).
lessons.cost: No interest from ante 4 on and no money at the ante 4-5 point where the playbook says to convert to xMult. The run was stuck and could not respond.

lessons.rule: Do not skip both blinds of an ante into a boss below 50%. A tag that only pays after the boss (Coupon, Polychrome) does nothing for the boss itself. When broke, play the Small Blind for its shop and the money from unused hands, and take free planets for the main hand or Pair from a Meteor pack.
lessons.evidence: At decision 52 it skipped the Small Blind at 85%, and at decision 54 it skipped the Big Blind for a Coupon Tag. That sent it into The Hook at about 10% with no shop in between. At decision 27 it had itself called this forbidden. At decision 53 it took nothing from a free Mega Celestial pack.
lessons.cost: It gave up two shops, the blind money and its last chances to improve the board before the boss that ended the run.

summary: The run got through antes 1-4 on flat scoring: Green Joker growth, Sly, an eternal plain Joker and a rented Ice Cream. It reached ante 5 with no xMult and Pair at level 2, and died on the first blind of ante 5 (the outlook gave it 12%). From decision 36 onward the outlook said ante 5 was 5-10%. Even so, the strategist kept ending ante 4 shops early to protect interest, sold its only xMult (The Idol) for Juggler, and spent its last money ($10 down to $0) only in ante 5, when it was too late. Earlier, $10 went on Telescope with no Celestial packs coming, a slot was locked by an eternal +4 Joker, and the Ice Cream rental cost about $15 in rent. Together these drained the money and slots needed to find a multiplier.

lessons.rule: If the outlook gives the next ante's Small or Big Blind below 20%, the interest floor no longer applies. Spend down to about $5-10 on rerolls and packs in the shops of the current ante that still have a blind after them. Hunt for xMult or main-hand planets now, not after entering the losing ante. The playbook's 'spend only above $25 unless the next blind would fail' should read 'unless any blind in the next ante reads below 20%'.
lessons.evidence: Decisions 36-50: ante 5 read 5-10% throughout. At 40 the strategist left the shop at $20 because 'a reroll drops two interest tiers'. At 44 it left at $16, and at 50 at $11, without rerolling. At 53-54 in ante 5 it spent $15 down to $0 (a reroll plus Grabber), when no shop was left to turn that into a working board.
lessons.cost: Roughly 3-4 rerolls (about 12-16 extra shop slots) were never seen in ante 4, the window where an xMult could still have saved the run. The money held for interest (around $4 a round) was worth nothing once the run died two rounds later.

lessons.rule: Never sell your only xMult joker for a joker that adds no score (Juggler, Splash, economy jokers). If a slot is needed, sell a flat joker, an expiring one, or a rental first. Treat a short-term outlook jump from a hand-size joker with suspicion when the next ante needs a multiplier.
lessons.evidence: Decision 39 sold The Idol (x2, conditional) for Juggler (+1 hand size) because The Club went from 60% to 95%. Ice Cream, a perishable rental with 3 rounds left, was the obvious sale instead. The board entered ante 5 with zero xMult (decision 52: 'no xMult', Small Blind 12%).
lessons.cost: It removed the only multiplier source. That left a purely additive board scoring about 4,000 a hand against a 25,000 blind.

lessons.rule: With 5 joker slots, do not take an eternal flat +Mult or +Chips joker after ante 2. A locked slot is worth more than +4 Mult once you need room for xMult. Skip the pack instead.
lessons.evidence: Decision 30 took an eternal Joker (+4 Mult) from a Jumbo Buffoon pack, when the Wall already read 95%. By decision 37 all 5 slots were full and that one could never be sold. That is why decision 39 had to sell The Idol to make room.
lessons.cost: One slot was locked permanently at +4 Mult. This led straight to losing the xMult and limited what later pack picks could do.

lessons.rule: Sell a rental as soon as the blind you rented it for is behind you, unless the outlook shows you still need it. Before buying a rental, count its total cost as $3 times the rounds you will keep it, not its sticker price.
lessons.evidence: Decision 28 bought the Ice Cream rental for $1 to get through the Wall (10% to 97%), which was reasonable. It was then kept through the Wall and all three ante 4 rounds while it shrank from 100 to 15 chips. It was sold only at 52, already expired and debuffed.
lessons.cost: About $15 in rent. That is the difference between having about $25 or more and having $11 going into the ante 4 boss shop, and roughly three rerolls that never happened.

lessons.rule: Do not buy Telescope (or Observatory) before you are actually seeing and buying Celestial packs. Below the hand-level target, spend the $10 on direct planets for the main hand, Celestial packs, or rerolls for xMult. Telescope pays only if you open about 3 or more Celestial packs after buying it.
lessons.evidence: Decision 21 bought Telescope at $28, dropping to $18, with Pair at level 1. Celestial packs were missing from shops 24, 25, 31, 34, 43 and 44. The first one opened was at 47 (ante 4 boss shop), giving one Mercury. Pair was still level 1 after 18 plays at ante 4 and level 2 at ante 5, against a target of 3-5 and then 6-9.
lessons.cost: $10 (two interest tiers in ante 2) for one guaranteed Mercury. Main-hand levels, the second-strongest engine, never came.

summary: Space Joker came from the first pack (decision 3). It levelled Pair to level 13 almost for free, so the second engine was more than done by ante 4. The run still never found a reliable xMult. Through antes 3 and 4 the strategist protected a $25–28 interest floor and left most shops without rerolling, even though the outlook already showed the next ante's boss at 0–30%. It finally spent the bank on rerolls in ante 5 ($28 down to $7), too late to find anything. It then lost to The Eye at about 11%: with no xMult and only one Pair allowed, it could not reach 50,000.

lessons.rule: If the outlook puts the NEXT ante's boss below 50% and the board has no xMult, spend down to the $25 tier on rerolls and Buffoon packs in every shop of the current ante. If it reads below 30%, go down to about $10. Do not save the money for when that ante arrives. An interest floor is only worth keeping while the run's survival two antes ahead looks good.
lessons.evidence: At #21 the outlook showed the ante 4 boss at 0%. Even so, #22, #25 and #30 left ante 3 shops at $25–27 without a single reroll. From #32 to #42 the ante 5 boss read 20–40%, yet #35 and #39 left shops because a reroll would drop money below the $28 floor. Ante 4 got only 3 rerolls. Then ante 5 (#46, #47, #52, #56) burned $28 down to $7 on 4 rerolls with only 2 shops left before The Eye, and found no xMult.
lessons.cost: About 5 shops in antes 3–4 went unrolled, and that was the window where the playbook says to buy the multiplier. The run reached the ante 5 boss with zero xMult and died there. The interest it saved bought nothing.

lessons.rule: Do not buy a rental joker before ante 5, even at $1, unless the next blind reads below 70% without it. A rental costs $3 every round, and it raises the money floor to $28. That floor then blocks rerolls for the rest of the run.
lessons.evidence: #21 bought Green Joker as a rental while the current ante read 90–100%. The strategist's own reasoning at #19 had said 'none before ante 5'. Over the next 9 rounds it charged about $27 in rent. The $28 floor it created was the reason given for not rerolling at #22, #25, #35 and #39. All it ever gave was +18 flat Mult.
lessons.cost: About $27 in rent plus 4 or more rerolls it blocked, roughly 6–8 extra shop looks for an xMult. It was the cheapest-looking buy of the run and one of the most expensive.

lessons.rule: Once the main hand is at or above its target level (Pair 7+ by ante 3), stop counting planets or Pair-only jokers as progress. Put all surplus toward an xMult. Loyalty Card does not count as one: with 4 hands it fires about once every 1.5 rounds, and it may not fire at all against a boss.
lessons.evidence: Pair was level 7 by ante 3 and level 13 by ante 5, but one Pair still scored only about 17.8k at #56. #43 bought Loyalty Card as 'a real multiplier'. At The Eye it had 5 hands left to count, so it could not fire (#56), and the board effectively had no xMult. #51 swapped Space Joker for Supernova, which adds +Mult, not xMult.
lessons.cost: The board had about 0 working xMult against a target of 1 by ante 5–6. The ante 5 boss read only 15–25% from the moment the ante began.

lessons.rule: Insure against hand-restricting bosses (The Eye, The Mouth) with cheap backup hand levels. When a free or already-opened Celestial pack offers no main-hand planet, take the planets for related hands (Two Pair, Three of a Kind, Full House) instead of skipping. Do not skip a blind in antes 2–4 for a planet tag, because that throws away a shop that could show an xMult.
lessons.evidence: #15 skipped the ante 2 Small Blind for a Meteor Tag. That gave up a shop and about $3. Then #16 skipped the entire Mega Celestial pack because it had no Mercury. At The Eye (#57–58), every hand except one Pair was level 1, so the 3 remaining hands added only a few hundred chips each toward 50,000.
lessons.cost: A lost shop in ante 2 and zero backup levels. Even a few levels in Two Pair or Three of a Kind would have raised The Eye's 11–25% clear chance.

summary: The run never built an engine. Pair stayed at level 2 from ante 2 through ante 4. The only lasting multiplier was a fading Ramen (x2 down to x1.82), and from ante 3 on the outlook kept showing the next ante at 0%. Money went to short-term patches: a perishable Supernova, a rental Wily, a perishable Golden Joker, and packs opened only to skip them for Red Card. Slots went to eternal flat jokers (Mystic Summit, Swashbuckler, Walkie Talkie). It reached ante 5 with $7, three of five slots locked, and no second multiplier, and lost the Big Blind it had read at 15-34%.

lessons.rule: Lock at most one slot with an eternal joker before ante 5, and only for an xMult or a scaling joker that fits the main hand. Never buy an eternal flat or conditional +Mult/+Chips joker when it would make two or more eternal slots, unless the next blind reads below 50% and nothing else fixes it. Before buying a flat joker in ante 3 or later, check that a free slot will be left for the xMult the run still lacks.
lessons.evidence: Decision 16 bought Mystic Summit as an eternal. It needs every discard used, which works against Ramen (decision 32) and later Blue Joker (decision 65). Decision 44 bought Swashbuckler as an eternal; it only adds the sell value of the other jokers, a few Mult. Decision 69 sold Loyalty Card for an eternal Walkie Talkie, the third locked slot. On the ante 5 Big Blind the board had 3 of 5 slots that could never be sold, all flat scorers, and Mystic Summit undercut the xMult and chips jokers next to it.
lessons.cost: No slot was left to convert to xMult in antes 4-5, which is the playbook's convert step. The final board read 26-34% on the Big Blind and 5% on the boss and died.

lessons.rule: Do not sell a working +Mult joker that is still growing for a trigger xMult (Loyalty Card, and similar every-N-hands jokers) unless the trigger fires on most boss attempts. Divide N by the hands you actually play per round. If it fires less than about once every two rounds, it is not a multiplier for planning.
lessons.evidence: Decision 51 sold Red Card (+9 Mult, still growing) for Loyalty Card. That ended the payoff from the $14 spent opening packs to skip them in decisions 25, 34 and 39. Loyalty fires x4 only every 6th hand, about every other round at 3-4 hands a round, so the outlook still read ante 5 Big at 10% and the boss at 0%. Six decisions later (69) it was sold again for Walkie Talkie.
lessons.cost: Lost a lasting +9 Mult and the money spent growing it, paid two swap costs, and gained no reliable multiplier for the ante 5 cliff.

lessons.rule: From ante 3, do not open a pack just to skip it for Red Card (or a similar skip trigger) when that takes money below $25. Open a pack below $25 only when it can plausibly hold the main hand's planet or an xMult joker. Every $5 below $25 costs $1 of interest every round.
lessons.evidence: Decision 34 opened an Arcana pack at $15 (down to $11) and decision 35 skipped it, both just to feed Red Card. Decisions 25 and 39 opened Celestial packs that missed Mercury and were skipped. In ante 3 money went from $34 (decision 23) to $11 (decision 36). Antes 3-4 ran at $7-15, about $2 of interest a round instead of $5. Ante 5 then began at only $28 and ended at $7 after the emergency rerolls (decisions 64, 66, 70).
lessons.cost: About $10-15 of interest lost across antes 3-4. Every one of those dollars could have been a $5 reroll looking for xMult while rerolls were still cheap. The +Mult it bought was sold anyway at decision 51.

lessons.rule: When the outlook shows the next ante at 0-10% for two antes in a row, the build lacks a multiplier, and planets or perishables will not fix that. Stop buying perishable or rental stopgaps (they expire just when needed). Spend the surplus above about $15 on $5 rerolls looking for xMult in the current ante, not in the crisis shop of the failing ante.
lessons.evidence: From decision 29 on, the outlook read the next ante at 0-5%. The patches were the rental Wily (decision 28, sold at decision 33 after paying rent) and the perishable Golden Joker for $8 (decision 43, sold at decision 65 before it expired). Shops at decisions 45, 48 and 53 were left with no reroll. The xMult search only started at ante 5 (decisions 64, 66, 70), with rerolls at $5, $6 and $7 on $20 or less, which turned up nothing.
lessons.cost: The xMult search happened one ante too late and on almost no money. The run reached ante 5 with one decaying x1.8 Ramen and failed the playbook's target of one xMult by ante 4-5.

summary: The run kept getting through blinds that were already safe but never built an engine that would last. By ante 5, three of the five joker slots were held by Eternal jokers that only added flat Chips, flat Mult or money (Blue Joker, Reserved Parking, Raised Fist), and the remaining slots held perishables. The only multipliers it ever had were a perishable Blueprint and a perishable Duo, and both ran out just before the ante 5 jump the outlook had warned about since decision 17. The Pillar read 30-40% for the whole of ante 5, and Director's Cut had been passed over in ante 4 with $31-50 in hand, so the run had no boss reroll when it needed one and died there.

lessons.rule: From ante 4, if Director's Cut is in the shop and you have $10 above your interest floor, buy it before any reroll or pack. Do this especially when the current boss or the next ante's boss reads below 50%. A boss reroll is a lasting fix for both cases. Spending the same $10 on two rerolls is a gamble.
lessons.evidence: Director's Cut was in the shop from decision 30 to 36 while the strategist held $50 down to $31 and The Flint read 10%. It spent $11 on rerolls (34, 35) and then fixed The Flint with an Eternal rental Raised Fist (36), noting that Director's Cut 'only rerolls the boss'. In ante 5 The Pillar read 29-40% from decision 57 to 72, and the run died to it with no way to reroll. The playbook's step 5 says to buy a boss reroll voucher by ante 6.
lessons.cost: Probably the run. One reroll of The Pillar ($10) would have taken a roughly 30% boss to the usual 70-100% for a non-debuffing boss. It also would have made the Raised Fist lock unnecessary.

lessons.rule: Treat Eternal as a permanent slot cost. Before ante 5, hold at most 2 Eternal jokers that are not xMult, and keep at least 2 slots free for jokers you can sell or swap. If the next blind forces you to accept a third Eternal, take the one with the highest ceiling (an xMult, Hanging Chad, a retrigger), not flat Mult. Never take an Eternal rental for flat Mult when a non-rental fix such as a boss reroll exists.
lessons.evidence: Blue Joker was bought Eternal (4) and Reserved Parking Eternal (8). Hanging Chad, which the playbook says to always take, was passed at decisions 30, 32 and 34 because it was Eternal and rental. Two decisions later the strategist bought Raised Fist, also Eternal and rental (36). By decision 55 it said 'only Burglar and The Duo can be swapped'. It could not sell anything to make room for xMult, and every swap it later considered lowered the outlook (67, 69, 72).
lessons.cost: The board could not move into xMult in antes 4-5, which is the playbook's main win condition. It also paid a $3 rental every round, which kept money below the reroll budget late in ante 5.

lessons.rule: A perishable joker only fixes the blinds it will still be alive for. Count its remaining rounds against the first blind the outlook marks as failing. If it expires before that blind, it does not solve the problem: keep looking for a permanent xMult at the same priority, and keep money ready for it.
lessons.evidence: The Duo was bought at decision 26 with 5 rounds left, and Blueprint (14) was perishable too. The strategist treated the multiplier problem as covered. It expired at ante 5 Small (56), just before ante 5 Big and The Pillar, the blinds the outlook had flagged since decision 17. In ante 5 it then took more perishables (Burglar 53, Mystic Summit 56), and the plan note admits these 'expire soon'.
lessons.cost: It reached ante 5, the steepest step, with no xMult at all. Pair at level 5 with flat Mult could not get through The Pillar.

lessons.rule: Once the main-hand planet has come up in a shop, buy it there for $3 rather than chasing it through Normal Celestial packs. Only open a Celestial pack when you have $10 or more above your interest floor and nothing better to buy. Never let packs or rerolls crowd out a voucher that fixes the run.
lessons.evidence: The strategist opened 6 Celestial packs (decisions 9, 23, 30, 32, 39, 42) for $26 and got 2 Mercury. Shop Mercurys came at $3 each (17, 58). Pair ended at level 5, below the 6-9 target, and two of those packs were bought in the same ante 4 shops where Director's Cut sat unbought.
lessons.cost: About $18 more than buying levels directly, which is nearly two Director's Cut purchases. It still left Pair under target at ante 5.

summary: The run reached ante 7 with Green Joker, Sly, Acrobat and Ancient Joker, and it levelled Pair from 1 to 8 using Telescope and Celestial packs. It never found a reliable xMult. Acrobat only fires on the final hand, and Ancient only on a suit that changes each round. Money fell from $37 in ante 3 to under $10 for all of antes 5-7, so the run rerolled only twice all game. By ante 6, five of the six jokers were eternal, which locked the board. At ante 7 the best hand scored about 22k against a 165k Big Blind, and there was no money and no sellable slot to change that.

lessons.rule: Don't take an eternal joker that only adds flat +Mult or chips once you already hold 2 or more eternals in normal slots. By ante 5, keep at least 2 non-eternal slots you can sell, so the 'convert to xMult' step (playbook antes 5-6) stays possible. An eternal sticker is fine on a real xMult joker but not on a flat filler.
lessons.evidence: Decision 16 took Acrobat (eternal) and 23 took Ancient (eternal). Then 53 bought Fibonacci (eternal) for $11 and 68 bought Supernova (eternal). From 81 to 86 the strategist notes that five jokers are eternal and Green Joker is the only one it can sell. Swapping out Green Joker would drop the blind from 97% to 12%, so no xMult could ever be added.
lessons.cost: The run couldn't convert in antes 5-7. The board ended with lots of +Mult (Green 47, Supernova 47, Fibonacci) but no steady xMult and too few chips, about 7x short of the ante 7 blinds.

lessons.rule: Until the board has one reliable xMult joker (one that fires every hand), spend the surplus above $25 in antes 3-4 on shop rerolls and Buffoon packs. Don't spend it on planet infrastructure. Buy Telescope or Celestial packs only once an xMult is on the board, or when the current ante's blind would otherwise fail.
lessons.evidence: There were only 2 rerolls in the whole run (decisions 9 and 39). Pair levels took about $38: Telescope for $10 at decision 30, plus Celestial packs at 43 ($8), 49, 54, 64, 69 and 77 ($4 each). Pair reached level 8, but each level adds only +15 chips and +1 Mult. The outlook kept showing a cliff one ante ahead (37, 43, 53, 68, 81) because the multiplier was missing. The playbook measures one x3 joker at +2.5 blinds against +1.3 for +6 levels.
lessons.cost: Money that could have paid for 6-7 rerolls searching for xMult went into levels that only nudged the boss odds. The run died in ante 7 with no xMult.

lessons.rule: Once you're at ante 4, do not let money drop below $20 while the current ante reads 95%+. Spend only the surplus above $25 (above $28 with a rental), so that at ante 5 you can still buy a fix without going broke. If the next ante already reads under 20% and you're below $25, use the safe ante to look for an xMult. Don't spend that money on extra planets.
lessons.evidence: At decision 39 a reroll took money from $29 to $24. At 43 a Celestial Mega pack took it from $25 to $17 while the outlook read 99%/95%. Ante 5 then opened at $20 against a boss at 0%. Survival buys (53, 54, 60, 64) brought money to $3, and it stayed between $0 and $7 through antes 5-7. The playbook says 'No rerolls for 2-3 antes means the run is in trouble', and that is what happened here.
lessons.cost: About $4-5 of interest lost each round for roughly 9 rounds. There was no money for rerolls in antes 5-7, and decisions 83 and 86 could not buy anything.

lessons.rule: Don't take a rental joker whose value grows with money (Bull) in antes 1-4 unless you will keep $28 or more. A $3 rent plus spending down makes it weaker every round. With Telescope, buy Normal Celestial packs, not Mega ones, unless at least 2 planets in the pack are on-plan.
lessons.evidence: Decision 22 took Bull (rental) from a free Mega Buffoon pack. It paid rent from ante 3 until it was sold at decision 56, when $5 in the bank made it worth only +10 chips. Decision 43 paid $8 for a Mega Celestial pack and took one Mercury, the same result a $4 Normal pack gave at decisions 49 and 54.
lessons.cost: About $12-15 of rent plus $4 of overspend, which kept money below interest tiers in antes 4-5.

summary: The run built a Pair engine early. Ride the Bus and Supernova supplied +Mult, Card Sharp gave x3, and Seeing Double gave x2 by ante 2, then Constellation was added at ante 5. Pair reached level 11 and the run got through ante 7. It never added a second permanent xMult or any chips source. It sold Seeing Double at ante 6 for a short-term fix. By ante 7-8 it had $0-6 and was spending $3 at a time on off-plan planets for +x0.1 on Constellation. It reached the Crimson Heart boss (400k) with one real xMult and about 165 base chips, and lost with a 0% read. The losses came from trading away permanent multiplier and from having no cash left for the last two shops, not from bad luck.

lessons.rule: Never sell a permanent xMult joker to buy a perishable or decaying joker (Turtle Bean, Popcorn, Ice Cream, Seltzer, Ramen), even if the sim says it fixes the current boss. If one boss needs a fix, sell a flat +Mult joker or spend money instead. From ante 6 on, the count of permanent xMult jokers should only go up (playbook target: 2+ by ante 7).
lessons.evidence: #73 sold Seeing Double (x2) for Turtle Bean to lift The Mark from 41% to 86%. Turtle Bean was down to +1 hand size by ante 7 and was sold for $3 at #100. Earlier, #52 had used an Arcana pick (The Moon, 3 cards turned to Clubs) only to feed Seeing Double, so that was wasted too. Ante 7 and ante 8 were played with Card Sharp as the only real xMult, and the ante 8 boss read 5-10% the whole time.
