lessons.cost: A permanent x2 on most Pairs (16 Clubs in the deck) during antes 7-8. That is about the gap between a 24% and a winnable Crimson Heart, and it left the board one xMult short of the playbook target.

lessons.rule: When the outlook says the final boss is at 15% or less, stop buying +5% steps such as off-plan planets for Constellation x0.1 ($3 each). Also stop trial buys that get sold right away. Keep $10 or more for the last two shops and spend it only on things that can multiply the score: a reroll or Buffoon pack aimed at an xMult or big-chips joker, or a Mercury.
lessons.evidence: In ante 7 the run bought Mars, Saturn, Neptune and Neptune again (#89, #101, #104, #114), each just for +0.1 on Constellation. It made four rerolls (#93, #94, #103, #106) that found nothing. It bought Splash and sold it one decision later (#107-108). Money went from $26 to $0 at #117, then $2 in ante 8 (#121-122). It could not afford Mars, a Celestial Jumbo, Hieroglyph, a reroll or a Buffoon pack in the final shops (#122, #133). The ante 8 boss stayed at 5-10% through all of this.
lessons.cost: The last two shops before the run's deciding boss went unused. The ante 8 boss reached only 24-33%.

lessons.rule: Once the main hand is chosen and you expect to buy several Celestial packs (or play Constellation), buy Telescope when it shows up in antes 2-4, even if it costs one interest tier. Each missed Mercury costs a $4-6 pack. The playbook's 'Telescope -> commit harder' signal should rank Telescope above holding $25.
lessons.evidence: Telescope was offered at #13, #17 and #21 (ante 2, $11-16) and passed for interest. Later Celestial packs missed Pair's planet at #32, #92, #113 and #129-130. That was 5 packs, about $26, that gave only off-plan planets. Pair finished at level 11, short of the ~12 target, and chips stayed around 165.
lessons.cost: About 4-5 Pair levels (+60-75 chips and mult on every hand) and roughly $20 wasted on packs that missed.

lessons.rule: From ante 5, if the board has two or more +Mult jokers and an xMult but no chips joker, and the main hand gives under ~200 chips, rank a chips source (Castle, Stuntman, Bull, Hiker, Ice-free Blue Joker, Arrowhead, Odd Todd/Scholar for Pair) above another +Mult or planet. Look for one with the surplus money in antes 5-6, not in ante 7.
lessons.evidence: At #107 and #120 the strategist itself said chips (~145-165) were the small side against ~100 Mult times x3 times x2. The board never held a chips joker. Ride the Bus, Supernova and Misprint (#124) were all +Mult, and Splash, the only attempt at chips, was sold at #108. Meanwhile, $11 of ante-5 rerolls (#53, #56) and the ante-5 surplus went into one Arcana pack and Mercury.
lessons.cost: Score was capped by the chips side. Doubling base chips would have roughly doubled the score, enough to move the Crimson Heart read from about 24% toward a likely clear.

summary: The run had a good early start. Holo Burglar, Hiker and Constellation, fed by cheap planets, carried it through the first antes. Card Sharp gave it a second xMult at ante 4 and Pair reached level 6. Two vouchers (Hieroglyph, then Petroglyph) sent it back two antes. It then ruined itself in two places. At decisions 65-71 it spent all its money ($17 to $0) because of an outlook reading that it had already called a glitch. Then at The Arm (120) it kept playing Pair, which dropped Pair from level 6 to 2 right before the ante 6 jump. It reached ante 6 broke, with no Director's Cut. It had paid $10 for Observatory, which did nothing. The Eye made Card Sharp useless, and the run died there.

lessons.rule: Against The Arm, never play your levelled main hand. Before the round, name one off-plan sacrifice hand (High Card or a spare hand), lock the round player to it, and clear in as few hands as you can. Hold Pair planets and any Fool until after The Arm, then use them.
lessons.evidence: At 120 the style was set to Two Pair, but Pair went from 34 to 40 plays and dropped from level 6 to 2. Card Sharp's 'repeat the hand' logic and Burglar's 7 hands made things worse, because every repeat cost a level. The note at 107 said to keep The Fool for after The Arm, but it was used at 115, before The Arm.
lessons.cost: Four Pair levels, roughly $12-16 of planets and the main payoff of Telescope. Ante 6 opened at Big 30% / Eye 5% with Pair at level 2 against a target of 6-9. This was the decisive mistake.

lessons.rule: If an outlook number suddenly jumps or drops with no change to the board or the blind, and especially if you flagged that number as an artifact earlier, check it first: re-query it or compare it with the round player's clear estimate. Do not use it to trigger the 'survival overrides interest' rule and spend everything.
lessons.evidence: At 58 and 60 the strategist wrote that the 12% reading 'looks like an engine artifact'. At 65-71 that same 12% for The Wheel triggered a full spend from $17 to $0 (Jumbo pack, reroll, Mercury, Saturn). At 73 the round player put The Wheel at about 100%.
lessons.cost: $17 of bank plus about 3-4 rounds of lost interest. Money stayed below $25 for most of the repeated antes ($10, $17, $23), so there was less to reroll for xMult later.

lessons.rule: Buy a voucher only if it works with the engine you already have. With Constellation, planets get used right away, so Observatory (which needs planets held in the 2 consumable slots) is dead money. With Card Sharp or Burglar repeat plans, buy Director's Cut by ante 5-6 so you can reroll bosses like The Eye, The Arm and The Psychic.
lessons.evidence: At 102, $10 went to Observatory, and every planet afterward was used immediately (116-117, 122, 133). At 127 and 137 the strategist could not afford Director's Cut against The Eye, which turned off Card Sharp. Hieroglyph and Petroglyph (53, 64) cost another $20 and pushed money down to $15-17.
lessons.cost: $10-30 that could have bought Director's Cut. With it, the ante 6 boss would have been rerollable instead of a 10-17% wall.

lessons.rule: Under the severe-forecast exception, spend the surplus only on things that can directly add xMult or main-hand levels: joker rerolls, or Celestial packs with Telescope. Never spend below about $15 going into the cliff ante, plus $3 for each rental. Spectral and Arcana packs and one-card tarots do not count as fixing a forecast.
lessons.evidence: From 109 to 113, money went from $30 to $9 on two rerolls, a Spectral pack (Grim gave 2 Aces) and an Arcana Jumbo (another Fool). None of it added a multiplier. Ante 6 started at $13 and dropped to $6, $3 and $2, with Card Sharp rent due (124-137). No rerolls were possible in the ante that killed the run.
lessons.cost: No shop power at all in ante 6. The final shops were spent selling jokers to cover rent.

lessons.rule: Do not skip for a Rare Tag (or Buffoon/Uncommon Tag) unless a joker slot is free, or you have already chosen a weak non-eternal joker to sell for it. Do not buy eternal utility jokers that permanently take a slot from the xMult conversion.
lessons.evidence: At 119 the Big Blind was skipped for a Rare Tag while all 5 slots were full, and one of them was eternal Riff-Raff, bought at 50 for $8 and needing empty slots to do anything. At 125 the strategist noted that all 5 slots were full, and no rare joker appeared on the board. The skip also gave up the Big Blind payout and a shop while at $9.
lessons.cost: The skip lost about $10 (payout, unused hands, interest) and a shop, with nothing in return. One of the 5 slots was locked for the rest of the run.

summary: The run died in ante 2 after 4 blinds, on the 1,500-chip Big Blind (outlook 96%). By then it had $6, every hand still at level 1, and a board where every joker was conditional, perishable or both: Crafty (Flush only, eternal), Sly (perishable), The Duo (perishable rental) and The Idol. About $22 of early money went to two Buffoon packs and two rerolls. That bought conditional jokers that worked on different hands, and the reroll before the Big Blind left too little cash to buy anything in the last shop. The loss on a 96% blind was partly bad luck, but even a win there would have met The Water at 30% and ante 3 at 0%. The run lost because it never got an unconditional scorer or a single levelled hand.

lessons.rule: In antes 1-2, do not reroll when it takes money below about $15. This applies even under a self-made 'thin-board exception': the playbook's line is no rerolls or packs below $20-25 early. If you hold a rental, keep at least rent + $4 for the next shop, so a Celestial pack, a planet or a cheap +Mult joker is still affordable there.
lessons.evidence: #4 rerolled at $14 to $9 and found only Crafty Joker. #12 rerolled at $13 to $8 while carrying The Duo's $3 rent and found nothing. At #15 the bot had $6 with rent due, could not buy the $4 Celestial pack, and left the last shop before The Water with nothing.
lessons.cost: $10 of rerolls produced no lasting scorer. This was most of the money that could have bought Mercury, a Celestial pack or a +Mult joker before the Big Blind and The Water. Interest also stayed at $1 a round all game.

lessons.rule: Pick the main hand (Pair by default) by the first Buffoon pick, and from then on buy only scorers for that hand or unconditional ones. Do not buy an eternal joker for a different hand type just because it is 'the only scorer on offer'. An eternal can never be sold, so it takes a slot for the whole run.
lessons.evidence: #5 bought Crafty Joker [eternal] (Flush, +80 chips). #9 took Sly (Pair) and #11 The Duo (Pair). After ante 1 the hands played were Flush 3x, Two Pair 3x, Full House and Three of a Kind, all level 1. The Flush and Pair jokers never fired together.
lessons.cost: The run spent $4 and a permanent slot on a joker that is dead on the main hand. The bot's own plan note had to 'accept' the weak eternal going into ante 3.

lessons.rule: An early conditional xMult (The Idol, The Duo, and the like) counts as a finisher, not a base. Until there is one unconditional +Mult or chips joker, or a levelled main hand, rank cheap unconditional scorers and main-hand planets above conditional or perishable jokers in shop and pack decisions.
lessons.evidence: #3 took The Idol over the alternatives on an empty board. #9 took perishable Sly with 5 rounds left. #11 took The Duo, perishable and a rental. By #16 every joker was either conditional (Crafty, Idol) or expiring (Sly, Duo), and the plan note admits 'I need permanent Pair chips/Mult replacements'.
lessons.cost: The board had no floor. Outlooks swung between 5% and 30% for The Water and stayed near 0% for ante 3, so even a won Big Blind left the run almost dead.

lessons.rule: Reach main hand level 2-3 by ante 2, as the playbook targets. When the board is thin and money is under $10, a $3-4 planet for the hand you actually play, or a Celestial pack, is a better buy than a reroll or a second Buffoon pack. Track which hand you are really playing: if it is Two Pair, Uranus counts.
lessons.evidence: The bot bought no planets in 16 decisions. #6 passed Uranus while Two Pair was its most-played hand (3x). #10 passed the Jumbo Celestial at $7. #2 and #12 passed Earth. #15 could not afford the Celestial pack. It entered the 1,500-chip Big Blind with every hand at level 1.
lessons.cost: This broke the playbook target (level 2-3 by ante 2). One or two Pair or Two Pair levels would have pushed the 96% Big Blind toward certain and lifted The Water above 30%.

summary: The run died to The Fish, the ante 2 boss, after 5 blinds. Ante 1 ended with Photograph (x2 on the first face card), Ice Cream (+100 chips that shrink by 5 per hand) and only $4, because a reroll and a $5 buy took money from $14 down to $4. In ante 2 the board kept getting more chips (Sly Joker) and small extras (8 Ball, Dusk) but never a flat +Mult joker. The Fish read 10-25% from the first ante 2 shop to the end, and none of the purchases raised that number in a meaningful way.

lessons.rule: Before buying a scorer, multiply it out: score ≈ (hand chips + joker chips) × (hand mult + joker mult) × xMult. If chips are already about 10 times mult or more (for example 100+ chips against Pair's x2-3 mult), the next buy must be +Mult, not more chips. Pass on chip jokers in that state unless nothing else is on offer and the next blind would fail without it.
lessons.evidence: Decision 5 bought Ice Cream (+100 chips) and decision 14 bought Sly Joker (+50 chips), so the board had about 150-170 chips against x3 mult. Decisions 18, 21 and 25 then say themselves that the board 'lacks Mult'. Sly lifted The Fish only from 10% to 15%. A +4 Mult joker on the same board would have added roughly 2.5 times the score that +50 chips did.
lessons.cost: Both ante 2 joker buys went to the wrong side of the multiplication, and The Fish stayed below 25% to the end of the run.

lessons.rule: In ante 1, do not reroll when it takes money below about $15. After a Buffoon pack, if the shop has no scorer, keep the cash for the next shop and its interest. Yellow Deck's extra $10 pays for one early pack, not a pack plus a reroll plus a buy. Never finish ante 1 with less than $10 unless the next blind would otherwise fail.
lessons.evidence: Decision 4 rerolled at $14 (the playbook says no rerolls below $20-25 early) while the outlook read 97-100% for the rest of ante 1. Decision 5 then spent $5 on a decaying joker, leaving $4. Ante 2 began at $14 instead of about $25, so at decisions 18 and 25 the strategist could not afford rerolls or follow-up buys.
lessons.cost: About $10-15 of buying power and $2-3 of interest lost before the first real wall. That money could have bought the +Mult joker or packs the board needed in ante 2.

lessons.rule: When a boss two or more blinds away reads below 30%, rank each possible purchase by how much it raises that boss's outlook per dollar. If a buy adds less than about 10 points, it is not a fix; save the money for the next shop or pick a different option. Small Blind and Big Blind shops are where the boss is fixed, so look harder there (a reroll or pack aimed at +Mult) than in the last shop before the boss.
lessons.evidence: The Fish read 10% at decision 13 and 15-25% through decisions 14-26. Sly took it from 10% to 15%, Dusk left it at 19%, and selling 8 Ball and rerolling left it at 18%. At decision 15 the strategist left with $6 even though the boss read 15%. Decision 18 passed on a reroll at $8 because 'too little to buy' was left afterward. Then $13 went into the last shop (Buffoon pack, Dusk, reroll) when it was too late to look for anything better.
lessons.cost: About $20 spent in ante 2 for less than 10 points of boss outlook in total, and the run ended at ante 2.

lessons.rule: Do not pay $5 for a joker that shrinks with use (Ice Cream, Popcorn-type) when it would leave you under $5, unless the current blind would fail without it. Its value at the coming boss is what counts, not its value today.
lessons.evidence: At decision 5 Ice Cream was bought for its 100 chips while the outlook already read 97-100% for the Big Blind. By ante 2 it was down to 75 chips and still shrinking, and the strategist had to play around it ('clear in few hands') at decisions 17 and 20.
lessons.cost: $5 plus the interest it would have earned, and a joker slot used by a fading piece that did not help with The Fish.

summary: The run never built an engine. It reached ante 3 with no xMult joker, Popcorn running out, Swashbuckler and Sixth Sense doing almost nothing, and every hand at level 1. From decision 13 the outlook showed ante 3 failing (Big 10%, The Arm 0%) while ante 2 was safe. The strategist spent that safe ante on fruitless rerolls and left shops holding $11–15 instead of buying whatever would raise the ante 3 reads. In ante 3 it panic-spent ($8 Mega pack, $10 Grabber voucher), dropped to $1 and died at the Big Blind, with the boss reading 5–10% anyway.

lessons.rule: When the current ante reads safe but the next ante's Big Blind or boss reads below about 30%, treat it as an emergency now. In this shop, buy whatever raises those future reads: a planet for the most-played hand, or any +Mult/chips joker. Don't leave the shop with money unless nothing in it moves the next-ante numbers. The playbook's 'survival overrides interest' rule should apply to a forecast cliff one ante away, not only to the next blind.
lessons.evidence: Decisions 12, 16 and 20 all left the shop with $11–15 while ante 3 read 10%/0%. Decision 20 skipped Uranus (Two Pair, the hand played most at 5 times) and the Celestial pack to protect a $20 floor it wasn't even at. Decisions 22–23 then paid $8 for a Mega pack to get that same Uranus. Rerolls at decisions 15 and 19 cost $10 and bought nothing.
lessons.cost: About $10–13 wasted or idle in ante 2. Ante 3 started with every hand at level 1 and a 0% boss, and that caused the loss.

lessons.rule: Before ante 4, do not turn down a joker that scores because it is eternal or perishable when the forecast shows a failing blind. With an empty or near-empty 5-slot board, an eternal joker costs nothing. A perishable joker lasts 5 rounds, longer than a fading Popcorn. Only skip on stickers when the board is already safe for the next ante.
lessons.evidence: Skipped for stickers: Devious Joker (decision 12), Campfire (19), Walkie Talkie (26), and Supernova at $8 with The Arm at 5% (27). One shop later the strategist spent $10 on a voucher instead (30). It did buy an eternal plain Joker for $2 at decision 25, which shows eternal was no real cost.
lessons.cost: Lost three or four chances to add lasting Mult before the ante 3 cliff.

lessons.rule: In a failing ante, judge each purchase by how much it raises the boss read per dollar. Keep enough money (about $5–8) for the last shop before the boss. Don't spend the whole bankroll on a voucher that fixes the Big Blind but leaves the boss below 20%. Pick the cheaper scorer first, and sell the planned non-scoring joker before the boss.
lessons.evidence: Decision 30 bought Grabber for $10 at $11. The Big Blind went from 60% to 97%, but The Arm only went from 5% to 10%. Decision 31 then had $1, and the strategist couldn't buy or sell anything without lowering the reads. The sale of Sixth Sense planned at decision 29 never happened. Decision 27 had already turned down a $5–6 option.
lessons.cost: The pre-boss shop was gone and there was no money to fix The Arm. The run ended with $1 in the bank.

lessons.rule: Commit to the hand you actually play most, and buy its planets. If the record shows Two Pair (or any hand) played most often by ante 2, level that hand. Don't hold out for Pair planets because the playbook prefers Pair. The playbook's 'prefer Pair' advice is a default for choosing a hand, not a reason to turn down planets for the hand already in use. Keep the round style on that one hand instead of switching between Pair and Two Pair.
lessons.evidence: Decision 20 rejected Uranus because 'Two Pair isn't the plan' while Two Pair had been played 5 times. Decision 21 set the style to Pair, and decision 29 switched it back to Two Pair. All hands were still level 1 entering ante 3, against the playbook target of level 2–3 by ante 2.
lessons.cost: Missed the second engine from the playbook (main hand +3 levels is worth about +0.6 blinds), and later paid $8 for the same planet.

lessons.rule: In ante 1, don't reroll or spend below $5 to buy a joker whose only value is its sell price feeding Swashbuckler. Prefer a direct scorer from the current shop, or take the Pillar risk with what you have. Ending ante 1 near $0 wipes out the Yellow Deck's $10 head start.
lessons.evidence: Decision 4 rerolled at $12. Decision 5 bought Sixth Sense for $6 and dropped to $1. Money then peaked at $23 and never reached the $25 interest cap.
lessons.cost: About $4–5 of interest lost across antes 1–3, and no cushion when the ante 3 emergency came.

summary: The run died to The Mouth (18,000) at the ante 4 boss, with a 2% clear chance. It was lost in antes 1-2, when the strategist built a board where every scorer either decayed or charged rent. Ice Cream was a decaying rental, Acrobat a rental, Popcorn decayed and Zany was perishable. By ante 4 the rent was $6-9 a round, money never got above $21, Pair was still level 1 and Acrobat was the only multiplier. The outlook showed 0-10% for ante 3-4 bosses from ante 2 onward, but each fix was another short-lived or rented card rather than a lasting scorer, a Pair level or banked money.

lessons.rule: Before ante 3, do not take a rental joker unless the current blind reads below 50% and no non-rental option fixes it. Never hold 2 rentals while money is under $28. Before buying a rental, count its total rent (about $3 x rounds you will keep it) as part of its price.
lessons.evidence: #3 took the Ice Cream rental at ante 1 when Golden Joker was offered. #10 added the Acrobat rental, so rent became $6 a round. #35 added a third rental (an eternal Half Joker), so rent became $9 a round. Money went $21 -> $10 (#13), $8 (#33), $3 (#41). The playbook names 'bought rentals at ante 1' as a known past failure, and its rental rule is to hold $28 with one rental and $31 with two. Both were broken.
lessons.cost: About $40 of rent over 9 rounds, and no interest above $4 in any round. The money that should have bought Mercury planets, xMult rerolls and packs in antes 3-4 was gone, so by #36-#42 the strategist was gambling with $3-10.

lessons.rule: Count decaying and perishable jokers (Ice Cream, Popcorn, perishables, Seltzer) as zero when checking whether a boss two blinds or more ahead is safe. By ante 3 have at least 2 scoring jokers that do not shrink. If a decaying bridge is the only fix, buy it, then put the next spending toward something lasting rather than another bridge.
lessons.evidence: The ante 2 board relied on Ice Cream (100 -> 50 chips) and Popcorn (20 -> 4 Mult) (#3, #12). Zany was a perishable (#21). By ante 4 Popcorn read 4 Mult and Zany had 2 rounds left. The outlook had warned since #7 that the ante 2 boss read 5%, and later that ante 3 read 0%. Each time the fix only covered the current ante.
lessons.cost: The board was hollow when the steep ante 4 step arrived: about 50 chips, Onyx Agate and Acrobat against 18,000 under The Mouth (2%).

lessons.rule: Do not reroll in antes 1-2 when the current ante reads 100% and money is under $25. Use that money for the main hand's planet (Mercury for Pair) or bank it. If Pair is still level 1 at ante 3, buy any Mercury or Celestial pack on sight before rerolling. If packs keep giving another hand's planets, switch the style to the hand you have actually levelled.
lessons.evidence: #7 rerolled for $5 at $21 when ante 1 was 100% safe. #11 rerolled for $5 at $20. Both shops found nothing. Pair was still level 1 after being played 6 times at ante 4, against a playbook target of level 3-5 by antes 3-4. The packs gave Venus (#20) and Uranus (#31), which levelled Three of a Kind and Two Pair to level 2, but the round style stayed on Pair, so those levels were never used.
lessons.cost: About $10 of early rerolls (about $2 a round of lost interest). The main-hand level, the playbook's second engine, was never built.

lessons.rule: Do not skip the Big Blind when the boss after it reads under 50%. The Big Blind's payout and shop are the last chance to fix that boss. Skip a Small Blind only when the current board reads 100% through the next boss and money is at least $20, so the lost shop is not needed.
lessons.evidence: #25 skipped ante 3's Small Blind for a D6 Tag. The free rerolls in #28-#32 still found nothing. #42 skipped ante 4's Small Blind, and #43 skipped the Big Blind, going straight into The Mouth with no shop. The Big Blind option (49% x about 10%) was about 5%, against 2% for skipping. The Negative Tag's free joker would only appear in the shop after the boss, so it was useless here. The playbook lists 'skipped blinds' as a known failure.
lessons.cost: Two shops, the blind payouts and unused-hand money were lost in the deciding ante. The final boss was fought at 2% instead of about 5%, after one more shop.

summary: The run died at the ante 4 Small Blind. The board was holo Supernova plus a conditional Idol, Pair was still level 1 after 19 plays, and the best hand scored about 900 against a 9,000 target. The outlook flagged ante 3 at 5-20% from decision 9 and ante 4 at 10%/0% for the whole of ante 3. Two or three joker slots stayed empty the entire time. The strategist spent about $33 on six rerolls and two packs, but its buy list allowed only xMult, lasting chips or Mercury, so it turned down every cheap scorer that showed up. What lost the run was holding out for perfect pieces while the board fell behind, not a shortage of money.

lessons.rule: When the next ante reads below 30% and you have an empty joker slot, buy any affordable joker that adds score to your played hand now: +Mult, +Chips or a growing joker. Perishable, rental or 'stopgap' stickers do not rule it out. A perishable with 5 rounds covers the whole danger ante, and a rental costs $3 a round, less than a lost run. Keep the 'lasting pieces only' filter for when no slot is free or the forecast is already safe.
lessons.evidence: The strategist turned down Ride the Bus (#22), Smiley Face (#27), Mystic Summit (#29), Blue Joker for chips from the Jumbo pack (#35, taking Lucky Cat, a dead x1.0, then selling it in #36), Lusty (#39), Scary Face (#43) and Bull (#47/#51). Each time it cited perishable, rental or eternal stickers or an off-plan suit, while ante 4 read 10%/0% and 2-3 slots were empty. The playbook's antes 1-2 rule says to take whatever makes ordinary hands win now and to have 2-3 scorers by ante 3. The strategist applied the ante 3-5 'build the engine' filter too early.
lessons.cost: It reached ante 4 with two working jokers and a score about 10x short. Any two of the rejected jokers would have raised the Small Blind well above 12%, and possibly cleared ante 4.

lessons.rule: Set the bar for what you will buy before you reroll. If two rerolls in a row turn up only cheap scorers that you pass on, the bar is too high: lower it and buy the best scorer rather than rerolling again. Rerolling only pays off when the shop can actually offer something you will accept.
lessons.evidence: Ante 3 rerolls #22, #23, #27, #28, #37 and #38 ($33 total) each ended with 'nothing here helps'. In ante 4, #42, #43 and #46 added $18 more. Across these nine rerolls the strategist bought no joker. It then spent its last money on random consumables, Judgement and High Priestess (#44-#48), which add less score than a known +Mult joker.
lessons.cost: About $50 went to shop looks without adding any score. That would have paid for 3-4 cheap jokers or a dozen Celestial packs.

lessons.rule: When your main hand is 2 or more levels below the playbook target (Pair should be level 2-3 by ante 2 and 3-5 by ante 3), buy Celestial packs ($4) and Telescope ahead of rerolls ($5-6). Use any planet you get right away, or pivot to the hand that actually has levels. Do not let a second ante pass with the main hand at level 1.
lessons.evidence: Pair was played 19 times and stayed at level 1 into ante 4. Telescope was skipped as 'off-plan' at #7. Only one Celestial pack was opened (#20), and it gave Venus, which sat unused until the desperate #49. Mars was sold (#50). Planets are the playbook's second-ranked lever (+3 levels = +0.6 blinds, measured), and the strategist hardly chased them while rerolling six times for xMult.
lessons.cost: Pair scored with 10 base chips and x2 base Mult at ante 4. The board had nothing for Supernova's Mult to multiply, which made the 9,000 Small Blind hopeless.

lessons.rule: React to a bad forecast for the next ante while the current ante is still safe. If the outlook shows the next ante's boss below 30%, add one scorer in each shop of the current ante, even at the cost of an interest tier. The playbook's $25 hold from ante 3 assumes the following ante is roughly safe. Hold $25 only after the board already passes the next ante.
lessons.evidence: At #9 the ante 3 boss read 5%. The response was a single reroll, then leaving at $16 (#10). At #15 and #18 the strategist left with $14 and $23, passing Loyalty Card and other options to save toward $25. The only addition was a perishable Banner, which ran out exactly at the ante 4 cliff (#41). In ante 3 the Hermit (#32-#33) pushed money to $32, but it all went to rerolls and none to scorers.
lessons.cost: Two antes of shops (8 visits) went by with almost no lasting score added. Holding interest earned only a few dollars, which went to waste when the run died at ante 4.

summary: The run got through antes 1-4 on flat jokers (Bull, Mystic Summit, Misprint, Mad Joker, Blue Joker) and never found a multiplier. From ante 2 on, the outlook kept showing the next ante at 0-15%. At ante 5 the board had no xMult, and both Pair and Two Pair were only level 2 against a target of 6-9. The strategist spent about $55 on rerolls and $16 on packs and got back one chips joker. It also turned down every scaling or xMult option because taking one meant selling a flat joker and lowering a blind that already read 95%+. It went into ante 5 Big with $2 and a 12% read.

lessons.rule: If the outlook shows a boss within the next ante at ≤10% and the board has no xMult, stop guarding a current blind that reads 95%+. Sell the weakest flat joker for any xMult or scaling joker (Blackboard, Ride the Bus, Green Joker, Hanging Chad, Obelisk) as long as the current blind still reads at least ~75% after the swap. Keeping the flat board means losing at the next ante for sure. Do not skip a blind for a Buffoon/Mega Buffoon tag unless you are willing to sell a joker to take what it offers.
lessons.evidence: #19 turned down Hanging Chad, which the playbook says to always take. #20 turned down Obelisk. #33 skipped ante 4 Small for a Mega Buffoon tag, then #34 took nothing (Green Joker was offered) because 'every slot is full'. #37 turned down Blackboard, the only xMult offered all run, because selling would drop The Hook from 97% to 60-67%. #39 turned down Ride the Bus for the same reason. Meanwhile ante 5 read 0-15% the whole time.
lessons.cost: The run never had a single multiplier. The playbook measures one xMult as worth +2.5 blinds and the most important factor in winning. Skipping the blind at #33 also gave up a payout, interest and a shop for nothing.

lessons.rule: From ante 3, keep one joker slot free or sellable for the xMult you are hunting. Do not buy Eternal jokers (or a second Eternal) while the board has no xMult. An Eternal flat or utility joker takes a slot away from that search for the rest of the run.
lessons.evidence: #23 bought an Eternal Blue Joker, which filled the 5th slot with a flat chips joker, so every later find required a sell. #45 sold Misprint, the board's biggest Mult source, at ante 5 to buy an Eternal Astronomer. That added no score right before a Big Blind reading 30-38%, and the Celestial pack it was meant to make free could not be bought (#47).
lessons.cost: The full board caused the refusals in lesson 1. Astronomer gave up live scoring for setup that never paid off, and the Big Blind dropped to 12%.

lessons.rule: Spread rerolls across shops. Make at most 2 rerolls per shop, and never reroll if afterwards you can't afford a $6-8 xMult joker on top of your interest floor. If two shops in a row turn up nothing, put the rest of the surplus into planets or Celestial packs for the main hand.
lessons.evidence: #10-11 rerolled $28 down to $17 in ante 2, breaking the playbook rule of no rerolls below $20-25 early. #29-31 ran $5/$6/$7 rerolls in one shop, $44 to $26, right after the Hermit doubled the money. #41-42 went $21 to $10 at ante 5. #46 rerolled $7 down to $2, and #45 had already noted 'At $13 I can't buy an xMult after a reroll'. About $55 of rerolls found only Blue Joker.
lessons.cost: Rerolls ate the Hermit's $20 and the interest income. The run reached ante 5 too poor to buy any xMult that might have shown up, and too poor for planets.

lessons.rule: Pick one main hand by ante 2 and put every planet into it. When it is 2+ levels behind target (level 3-5 by antes 3-4), buy its planet whenever you see it and open Celestial packs before rerolling for jokers. The playbook's 'one Celestial look before a reroll' is too little when no xMult has turned up. Levels are the one engine you can buy reliably.
lessons.evidence: #9 levelled Pair (Mercury), then #28 switched to Two Pair (Uranus) because Mad Joker came from a random Top-up Tag, and #40 doubled down with Clever Joker. The strategist only opened two Celestial packs all run, one each in #8 and #27. At #27 it had $48 and still put $18 into rerolls instead of more planets. Ante 5 started with Pair at level 2 and Two Pair at level 2, against a target of 6-9.
lessons.cost: Each hand lost about half its potential levels. The measured value is +0.6 blinds per +3 levels, and the run had no second engine to fall back on when no xMult appeared.

summary: The run never found a lasting multiplier. It spent about $50 on nine rerolls across antes 2-4 and saw no xMult. Meanwhile the board kept turning over short-term jokers: Abstract, Riff-Raff, Popcorn, Swashbuckler and Seltzer were all perishable. The board leaned on face cards (Smiley and Scary Face) and Bootstraps, with Pair only level 3. It died to The Club, the ante 4 boss (18,000), whose win estimate had swung between 50% and 92% in the shops before it. The deciding failure was spending money on blind searches instead of lasting power, so ante 4 arrived with no engine.

lessons.rule: Only use the 'severe forecast, spend down to $15' exception when the current ante is not safe. If every blind in the current ante reads 95% or more, reroll only with money above $25, and stop at 2 rerolls per shop. Before any reroll, buy the certain upgrades first: a main-hand planet, a Celestial pack, or a Buffoon pack.
lessons.evidence: In #8-9 (ante 2, which read 100% throughout) two rerolls took money from $26 to $15 and found nothing. In #23 and #28 (ante 3, Small and Big at 100%) money went $25→$19 and $21→$16, again with nothing found. #36-38 rerolled from $43 to $25 for nothing. That is nine rerolls and about $50 in total. The forecast read 'cliff' every time, so the exception applied in every shop and stopped working as a limit.
lessons.cost: About $50 spent and several rounds below the $5 interest tier. That money could have bought 3-4 Mercury or Celestial packs, which would have put Pair at level 5-6 instead of 3 by the ante 4 boss.

lessons.rule: Hold at most 2 perishable jokers at once, and treat each one as a bridge only. Do not replace an expiring perishable with another perishable unless the current blind would fail without it. Prefer a weaker joker that lasts, or a scaling joker you can feed.
lessons.evidence: Abstract (#3), Riff-Raff (#6), Popcorn (#21), Swashbuckler, which was also a rental (#29), and Seltzer (#35) were all perishable. Most shop actions in antes 3-4 were swaps to replace jokers that were about to expire (#21, #35, #42), not additions to the build. The playbook says to take the first scaling joker and feed it; none was ever taken.
lessons.cost: Shop money and joker slots were spent standing still. The board reached ante 4 with no growth, and its strength depended on joker timers.

lessons.rule: Avoid a core scorer whose Mult falls when you spend money, such as Bootstraps, while the run still needs to buy its engine. Before the boss, read the lowest recent estimate for that boss, not the latest one. If any read in that ante was below 75%, spend in the last shop on something that counters the boss, even if it costs an interest tier.
lessons.evidence: #16 replaced Rocket with Bootstraps. In #47 the strategist rejected Judgement because spending would lower Bootstraps' Mult, and it left the shop on a 92% read. Reads for The Club in that ante were 50% (#39), 65% (#40), 75% (#42) and 85% (#44-45). The board relied on face cards (Smiley, Scary Face), and The Club debuffs the Club face cards. The round fell to 48% (#48) and the run was lost.
lessons.cost: The run ended at the ante 4 boss.

lessons.rule: While the board has no xMult and the next ante reads below 30%, do not skip a blind for an economy tag such as Investment. Every shop is a chance to find the multiplier. Skip only for a tag that directly shows jokers or planets, such as Buffoon or Charm.
lessons.evidence: #31 skipped ante 3's Big Blind for the Investment Tag, even though #25 had set the rule 'no skips while the next ante is collapsing'. The $25 it paid out was then spent on fruitless rerolls (#36-38). #11, the Buffoon Tag skip, was the better kind of skip, because it produced Smiley Face.
lessons.cost: One fewer shop before ante 4, plus the Big Blind payout. The $25 gained went into rerolls that bought nothing.

summary: The run died on the ante 6 Big Blind (90,000) with no xMult, Pair only at level 3, and $1 in the bank. Money never got above $21 and was never near $25. Two rentals cost about $30 in rent between ante 3 and ante 6 (Ice Cream about $9, Banner, which was also eternal, about $21). Shop money went on rerolls that found nothing ($21→$10 in ante 2, $17→$6 in ante 5). The rest of the time it sat at $11-13, too little to earn real interest, while the main-hand planets were skipped. By ante 5 it was too broke to buy what it needed (Hanging Chad at decision 52, Acrobat only after selling Drunkard), and the build had no multiplier for the ante 5→6 jump.

lessons.rule: Never buy an Eternal Rental joker. It can't be sold, so it costs $3 every round for the rest of the run, about $20-30 by ante 6. If a blind can only be saved with a rental, use a plain rental you can sell (like Ice Cream), or first check whether a main-hand planet or a pack buy saves it. If you do take an eternal rental, the playbook's $28 money floor applies from then on, and with no realistic way to reach it the purchase is a slow death.
lessons.evidence: #33 sold the shrinking Ice Cream rental to buy Banner [eternal; rental] for $1 (Wheel 15%→85%). From then on Banner charged $3 every round: money went $16→$12→$11→$13→$17→$3→$5→$2→$3→$5→$1. At #49, #55 and #59 the reason given for leaving was 'owe $3 rent'. At #52 Hanging Chad ($4, which the playbook says to always take) couldn't be bought with $2. Banner also tied the board to Drunkard: selling Drunkard for Acrobat at #57 dropped the next blind from 60% to 12%.
lessons.cost: About $21 in Banner rent plus $9 for Ice Cream, and interest lost on top. That was the money for rerolls and planets in antes 4-5, which was the playbook's window to find xMult.

lessons.rule: In antes 1-2, when there are still one or two shops before the boss, do not reroll below $20. Buy the cheap scorer on offer now, even a suit-conditional +Mult, rather than leaving the shop and rerolling later. A low boss read early in the ante is not an emergency yet, because the blinds before it give you natural shops.
lessons.evidence: #8 left a shop with Lusty Joker on offer ($14, boss 10% ahead). #10-11 rerolled $21→$10 in the first ante 2 shop and found nothing. The natural shops then fixed the boss anyway: Lusty at #15 and Ice Cream at #19 took The Flint from 10% to 100%. In ante 5 the same thing happened: #44-45 rerolled $17→$6 in the first shop and only found a Mercury, which left $2-5 for the next two shops.
lessons.cost: $22 spent on rerolls with no joker found. It knocked money off the path to $25 in ante 2 and emptied the ante 5 budget that was needed for xMult or Hanging Chad.

lessons.rule: Below about $15, with no way to reach $25 within the next ante, interest is worth only $1-2 a round. Spend on main-hand levels (Mercury, Celestial packs, Telescope) instead of holding cash to protect a tier. Planets for the main hand come first whenever the main hand is below the playbook target (level 3-5 by antes 3-4).
lessons.evidence: Pair was still level 1 at the start of ante 4 after 21 plays, and only level 3 at ante 6 against a target of 6-9. #26 skipped Telescope at $11. #42 skipped a Celestial pack at $13 because '$9 drops an interest tier' (a $1/round difference). #36 and #39 left shops holding $11-12. #30 got Uranus instead of a Pair planet. Mercury was bought only at #35 and #46.
lessons.cost: Pair was about 4-6 levels behind target. By the playbook's own measurement, +3 levels is worth about +0.6 blinds and +6 levels about +1.3, enough to change the ante 6 Big Blind read from 12%.

lessons.rule: Don't fill a joker slot with a card that doesn't score, like Drunkard, unless a scorer depends on it. In antes 1-2 a Buffoon pack with no scorer is a skip. Every early slot and dollar should go toward the 2-3 scoring jokers the playbook wants by ante 3.
lessons.evidence: #3-4 spent $4 on a Buffoon pack and took Drunkard because it was free. The board then had only one real scorer (Supernova) going into ante 2, and The Flint read 10%. That set off the reroll and rental chain (#10-11, #19). Later Drunkard became a crutch for Banner, and selling it at #57 dropped the Small Blind to 12%.
lessons.cost: The ante 1 money ($13→$9) went toward a card that never scored. The weak ante 2 board that followed led to the forced rental and reroll spending that kept money below $25 for the whole run.

summary: The run won 17 blinds and lost to The Pillar in ante 6 at 38%. The board was five flat jokers and a perishable The Duo, Pair was only level 3, and the strategist had $2. The main cause was that it found no xMult by ante 5. It used the "severe-forecast exception" in every ante, so money kept dropping to $9-16 and it never held $25 for interest. Much of that money went on Celestial packs, and three of them were spent on Pluto for a backup High Card hand. A $3/round eternal rental at ante 4 ate the rest. When a real fix showed up (Blueprint at decision 63, $10), it couldn't pay for it.

lessons.rule: Only drop below $25 when the next blind or the current ante's boss reads under about 70%. A low forecast for the NEXT ante, read off the current board, is not an emergency. In antes 2-5 that forecast is almost always bad, so it cannot justify spending down every ante. Spend only the money above $25. After two shops in an ante with no xMult, stop and bank.
lessons.evidence: Ante 2 read 95-100% safe throughout. Even so, decisions 9, 11, 14, 15 and 18 used the exception on a forecast for ante 3, and money went from $34 to $9. The same pattern ran in ante 4 (30-34, 39-40: $37 down to $16) and ante 5 (46, 50: $25 down to $11). Money was at $25 or more only around decisions 6-11, 29-30, 38 and 46. The rest of the time it sat at $9-22.
lessons.cost: About $2-4 of interest lost every round over roughly 12 rounds, so $25-40 in total. With that money it could have afforded the Blueprint ($10) at decision 63, more rerolls in antes 5-6, and the money buffer the playbook asks for while holding a rental.

lessons.rule: Buy Celestial packs only to level the main hand. If a pack has no main-hand planet, count it as a miss: skip it or take the planet that is cheapest to waste, and don't treat it as a reason to buy another pack. Keep levelling one hand. Prefer buying the main-hand planet straight from the shop over opening more packs.
lessons.evidence: Decisions 8, 26 and 31 took Pluto (High Card reached level 4 but was played only 4 times), and decision 33 took Uranus (Two Pair, played 0 times). The strategist spent $24 on five Celestial packs (7, 9, 25, 30, 32, 40) and got only 2 Mercurys. Pair was level 3 at ante 6, against a playbook target of 6-9 by antes 5-6.
lessons.cost: About 3-4 lost Pair levels, which the gap study rates at roughly +0.6 to +1.3 blinds. It also used up the money that should have gone toward finding an xMult.

lessons.rule: From ante 3 on, don't buy a rental (and especially not an eternal rental) unless you will still hold $28 or more after buying it. Never buy one for a flat +Mult joker. Before buying an eternal joker, check that it won't lock a slot you will need for xMult later.
lessons.evidence: Decision 35 bought an eternal rental Half Joker at $22, leaving $21. That broke the playbook rule 'with one rental hold $28'. After that, money stayed at $1-21 and the $3 rent came out every round (decisions 59-63 mention rent). Together with eternal Stuntman, 2 of 5 slots were locked to flat jokers.
lessons.cost: About $18 in rent over 6 rounds, plus lost interest. In ante 6 the strategist was down to $1-2 with no rerolls, which the playbook calls 'the run is in trouble'.

lessons.rule: Start looking for xMult hard at ante 3, with Buffoon packs and $5 rerolls paid for from the money above $25, and keep the cash to buy one when it appears. Don't spend the run's money on rerolls in an ante that is already safe at ante 2 and then reach ante 5 broke. If the board has no xMult by ante 5, sell spent flat or economy jokers (Misprint, Gros Michel) early to pay for searching, not after the money is gone.
lessons.evidence: The ante 2 rerolls (11, 14, 15, 18) cost $21 and found only Stuntman. The first Buffoon pack after ante 1 came at decision 53, in ante 5 with $14. The only xMult, a perishable The Duo, arrived at decision 56 in ante 6. At decision 63 Blueprint ($10) was on offer at $2, and selling would not have covered it.
lessons.cost: The run reached ante 6 with no lasting multiplier. The gap study rates that as the biggest single factor (+2.5 blinds), and it ended the run at The Pillar.

summary: The run reached ante 4 without a single lasting xMult. The board was mostly perishable jokers, and from ante 2 on the outlook kept warning that they would all expire around ante 3-4. To fix that cliff, the strategist used its "severe-forecast" exception and rerolled 10 times for about $56. None of those rerolls found a multiplier, and money fell from $37 to $3-7. Planets were spread over Pair, Two Pair and Full House, so no hand was ever strong. When a foil Joker Stencil finally showed up, it cost every dollar left plus Sly Joker, and The House still read only 12%. It ended the run there.

lessons.rule: Only break the $25 interest floor to save the next blind, not to fix a forecast one or two antes away. When only a later ante reads low, reroll with the money above $25 and no more than 2 rerolls per shop. If three shops in a row miss the fix, stop rerolling and rebuild money so you can afford an xMult when one appears (Stencil $10, Cavendish, etc.).
lessons.evidence: Ante 2 shops were safe (95-100%), but rerolls 11 and 12 took money from $29 to $18. In ante 3 the current blinds read 85-100%, yet rerolls 22, 23, 25, 28 and 34 spent $29 and money went from $37 to $7 by decision 37. Ante 4 rerolls 42, 44 and 49 spent another $16. None of the 10 rerolls produced an xMult. The playbook says 'spend only the surplus above $25 unless the next blind would fail', and the strategist applied its exception to a forecast an ante or more ahead.
lessons.cost: About $56 of rerolls plus about $4-5 a round of lost interest over 6+ rounds. Without that, the strategist would have held $25-35 in ante 4, enough to buy Stencil without selling Sly and still buy planets or another joker. Instead it hit The House at $1.

lessons.rule: Count a perishable joker as a scorer for the current ante only. Never sell a lasting scorer to buy a perishable unless the current blind is failing without it. Once 2 perishables are on the board, the next joker bought must be a lasting one, even if it scores less now.
lessons.evidence: The board took five perishables: Shoot the Moon (8), Walkie Talkie (10), Business Card (18), Splash (24) and Even Steven (35). At 24 the strategist sold the permanent +4 Joker for a perishable Splash, which was debuffed and worth nothing by 54. From decision 9 on, the outlook flagged ante 3-4 at 0-15% because of this. Each fix was another perishable that expired just as the cliff arrived.
lessons.cost: Ante 4 started with only two lasting jokers, Hanging Chad and Clever Joker. That left the ante 4 blinds at 5-30% and forced the emergency selloff in 54-57.

lessons.rule: Commit to one main hand and keep the jokers matching it. Once you name a main hand, buy only its planet and jokers that score it. Do not open Celestial packs at or below $20 unless the main hand's planet is likely. If the jokers you actually own point to a different hand (for example, Clever Joker means Two Pair), switch the main hand at once and stop buying planets for the old one.
lessons.evidence: Pair was named the main hand and levelled at 13-14, but by ante 4 it had been played 0 times. Clever Joker for Two Pair was bought at 21, Uranus was taken at 32, Earth for Full House at 40 (a pack bought at $14 to $10), and Sly Joker for Pair later on. At 50 the main hand became Two Pair. The hand most played was Straight or Full House (3x each), with no enabler for either.
lessons.cost: No hand above level 3 by ante 4, against the playbook's target of 3-5 at antes 3-4 for one hand. That spread was worth about +0.6 to 1.3 blinds by the playbook's measurements. About $11 went on planets and packs for hands that were never the engine.

lessons.rule: On Yellow Deck, when holding $25 or more with the next boss safe, accept one rental if it is a lasting scaling or xMult joker. Then hold $28. A $3-a-round rental that keeps growing beats a chain of perishables that have to be replaced every 5 rounds.
lessons.evidence: At 6 the strategist had $25 and passed Green Joker because it was a rental. At 45 it passed Hologram (rental, xMult) for the same reason. The playbook's Yellow Deck section says one rental is easier to carry, and 'take the first scaling joker you see and feed it'. The strategist treated 'no rentals' as absolute. It then spent far more than $3 a round replacing perishables and rerolling.
lessons.cost: It passed up the only early chance at a lasting scaling scorer, and possibly a lasting xMult in ante 4. That left the board without a multiplier until the last shop.

summary: Antes 1-2 went fine with cheap flat scorers (Lusty, Banner, Misprint). From ante 3 the outlook kept showing the ante 4-5 bosses near 0%. The run never found a lasting every-hand multiplier, and Pair was still level 2 at ante 5 when the target is 6-9. The run's best bankroll ($37 at ante 3) went on a Director's Cut that was never used and on rerolls. The only lasting xMult it bought, Bloodstone, needs Hearts on a deck that never got more Hearts. The perishable Duo from the Rare Tag carried antes 3-4; when it expired the board fell from 95% to 12% at the ante 5 Big Blind, and by then the money had been spent too late to fix anything.

lessons.rule: Do not buy Director's Cut (or any boss-reroll voucher) while the outlook shows the next ante's ordinary blinds or boss below about 50% and the board has no lasting xMult. A boss reroll does not fix a missing multiplier. Buy it at antes 5-6, as the playbook says, and only once the board can beat ordinary blinds. Before then, put that $10 into xMult hunting (Buffoon packs, rerolls) or main-hand planets.
lessons.evidence: Decision 27: at $37, the most money the run ever held, it bought Director's Cut for $10 while its own reason said ante 4 read 5% and then 0% with no multiplier. The voucher was never used. At 38 and 51 the strategist turned down the $10 roll as too expensive, and at 65 it could not afford one.
lessons.cost: $10, plus about $2 a round of lost interest, at the moment the run most needed scoring. That is 2 Celestial packs, or a reroll plus a cheap xMult, in the shops just before the ante 5 cliff.

lessons.rule: When the outlook puts the next ante's boss at 10% or lower, or the board's only xMult is perishable and expires within the next ante, spend the surplus in the current ante's shops. Do not bank it at $18-20 and then spend everything in the shop of the ante you cannot beat. Each shop before the cliff should get at least one Celestial pack or main-hand planet. If the main hand is 3 or more levels below target, buy related-hand planets and Planet Merchant too.
lessons.evidence: Decisions 37, 43, 46 and 50 left shops holding $18-20 while the outlook read ante 5 Big 5-10% and Boss 0%. Mars and Square Joker were passed over at 46. Then 53-57 spent $18 in the ante 5 Small Blind shop: Mercury, two rerolls and a Spectral pack. Only 2 Pair levels were gained all run (decisions 15 and 54). Pair reached ante 5 at level 2 after 20 plays.
lessons.cost: This decided the run. Pair at level 2 with no lasting xMult cannot score 37,500. Spending the same money one ante earlier gives three or four more shops of chances, plus planet levels that apply to every later hand.

lessons.rule: Do not treat a suit-conditional xMult (Bloodstone, or any suit-based multiplier) as the permanent multiplier unless the deck is already tilted toward that suit, or you commit to tilting it with suit-converting tarots and Arcana packs. On an even 13/13/13/13 deck playing Pairs, it fires on only a small fraction of hands. Keep looking for an unconditional xMult.
lessons.evidence: Decision 40 sold Lusty for Bloodstone and called it the lasting multiplier. The deck stayed at exactly 13 Hearts all run. Arcana packs and tarots were skipped at 16, 55 and 63. At 55-62 the outlook still read Big 10% and Boss 0% with Bloodstone on board, so it added almost nothing.
lessons.cost: This was the run's only lasting-xMult purchase, and it did not stop the ante 5 collapse. It also used up a slot and money that the search for a real multiplier needed.

lessons.rule: When a perishable xMult is the board's main multiplier, count the rounds left on day one. Plan its replacement to arrive at least one shop before it expires: either a lasting xMult, or enough main-hand levels that the board reads 50% or more on the next ante's Big Blind without it. Do not 'keep interest' while a perishable is carrying the board.
lessons.evidence: Decision 36: The Duo came with 5 rounds left, and the reason noted that it covers exactly through ante 4. At 37 the strategist then chose to keep interest at $20 because the ante 4 boss was a 'mild' 60%. From 46 to 50, each reason noted that The Duo expires in ante 5, but no replacement was bought. At 62 The Duo expired and the read fell to 12%.
lessons.cost: Five rounds of warning were wasted. The board went from a 95% read to 12% in one blind.
